Research brief · 16 November 2026

Voice Capture Field Guide

Build an honest recorder that the user starts, for the Apple Watch people already own. Do not build a hidden 24/7 listener. watchOS lets a third-party app record for hours in the background only after the user taps in the foreground. Capture cannot resume after a call or Siri until the user taps again. The watch has no speech recognition and no on-device LLM, and low-level sockets are restricted. So the watch should be a thin, durable capture device, and the iPhone, a required companion, should do transcription and synthesis.

272 products in 11 categories · 126 fact-checked twice · 30 upcoming or rumored · 28 with an Apple Watch app

Where the opening is

The catalog shows capture and summaries are commodities: cloud transcription appears in 211 of 272 products and automatic summaries in 165. Trust tooling is scarce (consent and recording controls 76, local-only or end-to-end privacy 59), and few products capture on the watch (Apple Watch app 28). Apple sets the privacy bar with Siri Recap (summaries only, no transcript or speaker labels, deleted after 7 days unless saved) and Live Rewind (a 15-second transcript snippet). Both need a Series 12 or Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later, English, and a region outside the EU. That leaves room for:

  • cited full transcripts
  • separating the wearer from everyone else
  • retention that depends on jurisdiction and consent
  • support for Series 9-11, SE 3 and Ultra 2-3
  • an exit guarantee based on exported files

What could sink it

The biggest risks are still App Review treating the audio background mode as playback-only (forum 776949), battery drain nobody has measured, and wiretap and consent law.

Recommendation 1

The minimal always-on Apple Watch app

8 parts make a recorder worth wearing all day, plus 2 that are the first to go if time runs short. They are in build order. Each says what it does, why it made the cut, and how to build it with the APIs watchOS offers today. Marks such as [H], [M] and [L] give the research's confidence (high, medium, low) in a platform claim.

  1. One-tap foreground start (Session or Memo) with preflight, consent reminder and start cue

    The Start screen runs a preflight check. A Session then starts with one tap from a complication, a Smart Stack widget, a Control (Control Center, Smart Stack or the Ultra Action Button), or Double Tap on the Start screen, and it can be time-boxed. A Memo is press-and-hold on the in-app button. Starting a Session plays a haptic (plus a chime if it passes the device test) and shows a full-screen Recording state. A 2-second consent reminder appears at every Session start, with Announce offered (and pre-selected in strict jurisdictions). In the EEA, UK and Germany the Start screen offers Memo only.

    Why it's inA foreground start is the only legitimate path to long recording [H], and the trigger has to be close to effortless or the daily habit never forms. The preflight check matters because if notifications or the companion app are missing, the honest-gap design fails silently. The cue, indicator and reminder meet guideline 2.5.14, and they respect the EDPB position that consent obtained after recording is invalid.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Info.plist: UIBackgroundModes 'audio' and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription.
    • Preflight before Start:
      • Microphone record permission. If denied, Start is blocked.
      • UNUserNotificationCenter notificationSettings: authorizationStatus and timeSensitiveSetting. If either is off, show 'Interruptions won't alert you' and require an acknowledgement.
      • WCSession.default.isCompanionAppInstalled. If it is false, Sessions are blocked.
      • Free storage, and battery against the projected hours from measured history. Warn if the time box exceeds what is left.
    • Audio session: setCategory(.record) by default. Use .playAndRecord only if the chime and Announce pass the device test. Pass no .allowBluetooth (HFP) option, so input stays on the watch mic.
    • Activation: setActive(true) once per capture run, meaning Start or a user Resume. Never re-activate during silence or Pause. Then AVAudioEngine inputNode.installTap.
    • Entry points:
      • A WidgetKit accessory complication and a Smart Stack widget, both deep-linking with widgetURL.
      • A watchOS 26 ControlWidget whose intent opens the app. Controls run in the widget extension and cannot start capture themselves. The Ultra Action Button runs that Control.
      • Double Tap through .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction) on Start: S9 and later, not in Low Power Mode, not wrist-down.
      • Memo is a long-press gesture.
    • Cue: WKInterfaceDevice.current().play(.start). Option A adds a short bundled AVAudioPlayer clip. It ships only if a device test shows it plays in Silent Mode and on the built-in speaker with AirPods connected, without changing the input route. Option B (fallback) uses haptic, screen and the consent card only, with .record. The orange mic indicator is automatic.
    • Jurisdiction: read coarse location (reduced accuracy) on the watch or ask the paired iPhone at each Session start. Fall back to the onboarding answer, and treat it as strict when unknown. Write jurisdiction, reminded and announced_by into the session record.
    • Do not bind the Crown double-press (Live Rewind on Series 12 and Ultra 4).
    • No HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession keep-alive.
    • Do not depend on AudioRecordingIntent or a Live Activity [L].

  2. Speech-gated capture into encrypted 2-minute segments that survive a crash

    Once started, the mic stays open in the background with the wrist down. Only speech, with a short lead-in and tail, is encoded to AAC and written as ADTS in 2-minute segments. Files are protected at rest. Each segment is hashed and journaled, so a crash loses at most the last partial audio frame.

    Why it's inThis is the always-running core. Dropping silence cuts storage, radio use and phone transcription, and keeps less audio of other people. A crash-tolerant format and the journal are what make sync and recovery honest (compare Omi's 11-hour loss). An MP4 container cannot be read until it is closed, so it would not survive a crash.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Ring buffer of at least 4 s fed by the tap.
    • Energy gate: vDSP_rmsqv per 20 ms frame against an adaptive noise floor. Pre-roll is taken 2 s back from the moment the gate trips, not from the SoundAnalysis confirmation, so the confirmation delay (~1 s window plus processing) doesn't clip the first words.
    • SNAudioStreamAnalyzer with SNClassifySoundRequest(classifierIdentifier: .version1) confirms the 'speech' class. Unconfirmed audio is dropped after about 2 s. Hangover is 3 s.
    • Encoding: AVAudioConverter to AAC-LC, mono, 16 kHz, 32 kbps (24 kbps in Low Power Mode), written as ADTS (.aac, kAudioFileAAC_ADTSType). Verify that the writer is supported on watchOS. If it is not, use 60 s .m4a segments and accept a loss of up to 60 s on a crash.
    • Rotation every 120 s by wall clock, about 0.5 MB per segment. Rotation is also the heartbeat: intervals with nothing encoded still write a sidecar-only record.
    • File protection: create segments with FileProtectionType.completeUnlessOpen, so new files can be created after the watch locks. Fall back to .completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication if writes fail on lock (device test).
    • JSON sidecar per segment: session id, seq, wall-clock start and end, SHA-256, bitrate, bookmarks, pause, gap and discard markers, consent flags, input route, close reason.
    • Append-only journal, fsync'd at each rotation.
    • At launch, truncate an orphaned ADTS segment to its last complete frame, hash it, close it with reason crash_recovered, and write a GAP from that point to the relaunch.
    • Never stop or re-activate the engine during silence; gate only at the encoder.
    • SoundAnalysis is on by default only after its CPU cost is measured; the energy gate alone is the fallback.
    • Check onset clipping on a labelled sample. AAC only, because Opus on the watch is unverified.
    • Decision: the 3 s hangover sits between Proposal 1's 1.5 s and Proposal 2's 3-5 s.

  3. Delivery ledger with receipts and visible states

    Each closed segment goes to the iPhone, which writes it durably and confirms. If the iPhone stays unreachable, the segment goes to the user's CloudKit private database instead. The watch deletes a segment only after a confirmation. The app and complication show Recorded, Queued, On iPhone, Waiting for iPhone, Transcribed.

    Why it's inLost or never-transferred recordings are the top complaint in this category. Receipts and visible states turn silent loss into a status the user can see and retry.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Send each closed segment with WCSession.default.transferFile(url, metadata: [session, seq, sha256]).
    • Monitor outstandingFileTransfers and session(_:didFinish:error:). Re-queue failed transfers, and any still outstanding after 30 minutes.
    • The iPhone app is woken by WatchConnectivity. It checks the hash, writes the segment to the protected vault and confirms with transferUserInfo(['ack': [session, seq, sha256]]). It does no transcription during that wake. Do not use sendMessage, which fails when the iPhone app is in the background.
    • If the iPhone is unreachable and no ack has arrived for 15 minutes, save the segment as a CKAsset with CKModifyRecordsOperation to the user's private database, during the runtime the audio session already provides (DTS, forum 843751). A successful save counts as the receipt.
    • Leftovers retry in WKApplicationRefreshBackgroundTask (about 4 per hour with a complication on the face).
    • The iPhone imports through a CKDatabaseSubscription, de-duplicates by (session, seq, sha256) against the WatchConnectivity path, and deletes the CloudKit record after import. There is no vendor endpoint.
    • Decision: this follows the specific DTS guidance over the Earshot notes' 'always background', because background uploads may wait for Wi-Fi.
    • No sockets or WebSockets (TN3135; the path is revoked every ~36-38 s, FB24377808).
    • Test on hardware with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off. The Simulator does not support transferFile. CloudKit from a watch in a background audio session is unverified.

  4. Interruption detection, a dead-man's switch, honest gaps and one-tap resume

    When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app takes the mic, the app taps the wrist with 'Recording stopped by call - Tap to resume'. It then closes the segment, records a GAP with the reason, and shows Resume on the complication. If the app dies without any notification, a pre-scheduled alert fires within about 5 minutes and the complication turns to 'Check recording'.

    Why it's inCapture cannot resume from the background [H]. Without this, the app quietly stops at the first phone call, or at a crash or jetsam that it never sees, while the user believes the whole day was recorded. That is the worst failure possible.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Observe AVAudioSession interruptionNotification, routeChangeNotification, mediaServicesWereResetNotification and AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange.
    • On .began, do these in order:
      1. Post a UNNotificationRequest with interruptionLevel .timeSensitive (needs the Time Sensitive capability) and a 'Resume' UNNotificationAction with the .foreground option, before any file I/O.
      2. Finalise the segment and write a GAP {start, reason}.
      3. Reload widget timelines.
    • If the input port leaves the built-in mic: GAP and end the run.
    • Dead-man's switch: at every rotation, add a UNNotificationRequest with the fixed identifier 'deadman', a 300 s UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger and the text 'Recording stopped - tap to resume'. Adding a request with the same identifier replaces the pending one, so this reschedules it. Remove it on Stop, guard stops and Session end.
    • Complication timeline: built at state changes. It shows REC with Text(timerInterval:) and pre-schedules an entry ~20 min ahead reading 'Check recording - last confirmed hh:mm'. While alive, the app pushes that entry forward with one reload every 15 minutes (verify the reload budget).
    • Resume: the app opens to a full-screen Resume button with .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction). Resume starts a new capture run, calling setActive(true) and engine.start() as a user action in the foreground. Test URLSession and CloudKit uploads after a resume (FB24377808).
    • Send at most one follow-up reminder, after ~10 minutes.
    • Never try to restart in the background; it fails with 'Session activation failed'.
    • The iPhone passes GAP tokens to every summariser.
    • Soak tests on each model: kill the process, force memory pressure and jetsam, reboot, calls, Siri, timers with sound.

  5. Timed Pause that asks before resuming, and Stop

    Pause lasts 15 minutes by default (1 hour optional) and saves nothing. The screen says 'Paused - mic open, nothing saved' and shows the current time. When the timer ends, the watch taps and asks 'Resume recording?'. If nobody answers within 10 minutes, the Pause becomes a Stop. Stop turns the mic off and the orange indicator clears; restarting takes a foreground tap. Pause is the largest button on the recording screen and is also on the complication.

    Why it's inUsers must be able to honour 'please don't record' instantly, or they stop wearing the watch in social settings. Resuming without asking could quietly start recording again someone who objected. All-party consent law and the EDPB make this a compliance need too. Stop exists because the mic indicator stays lit while paused.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Pause sets a gate flag, so the tap callback drops buffers before the voice detector and encoder. The engine and session keep running, because re-activating from the background fails.
    • When the timer ends: play WKInterfaceDevice play(.notification), show a 'Resume recording?' prompt in the app, and post a local notification with a 'Resume' action (.foreground).
    • Resume is the Double Tap target. Because the engine is still running, Resume only flips the flag; no re-activation is needed. Verify that the notification action brings the app forward and flips the flag reliably.
    • If there is no answer within 10 minutes, run Stop and notify the user.
    • Auto-resume is a setting that is off by default and unavailable in strict jurisdictions.
    • Stop calls inputNode.removeTap, engine.stop() and setActive(false, options: .notifyOthersOnDeactivation), and cancels the dead-man notification.
    • GAP reasons: user_pause, pause_expired_stop, user_stop.
    • Decision: every pause is timed (Proposal 3), Stop is the real mic-off (Proposal 2), and resuming needs the wearer's confirmation. Double Tap is never bound to Pause or Stop.

  6. Discard recent audio (last 5 min, last 15 min, this Session)

    A Discard control on the recording screen and the complication deletes the last 5 or 15 minutes or the whole Session. It takes two taps and offers a 5-second undo. The watch drops the matching audio, and the iPhone deletes anything already delivered or derived in that range before it is transcribed or sent anywhere.

    Why it's inPause and Stop only prevent future capture. When a bystander objects to what was just recorded, the wearer needs to delete it then and there. Consent obtained after recording is invalid (EDPB), and Limitless's guidance says to delete audio captured without consent.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Never bound to Double Tap. Confirm with a second tap, and keep the deletion in memory for a 5 s undo before committing.
    • On the watch: clear the ring buffer, truncate or delete the open segment, delete unsent segments that overlap [from, to], and write a GAP with reason user_discard.
    • Write the tombstone {session, from, to, created} to the journal, so it is re-sent after a crash. Send it with transferUserInfo, which is queued and delivered.
    • On the iPhone, tombstones are applied before every transcription and egress step. They delete the audio, transcript spans, derived objects, search-index entries and any CloudKit copy in range, and add an entry to the consent log.
    • The cloud exit point sends nothing younger than 15 minutes, so a 15-minute discard always wins.

  7. Battery, storage and off-wrist guards with measured hours left

    The app measures this watch's drain during the session and shows about how many hours are left, or 'Measuring...' for the first 30 minutes. It drops to a lower bitrate in Low Power Mode. It stops cleanly at 15% battery, under 100 MB free, or when the watch is put on its charger, with a final haptic and notification.

    Why it's inA dead watch fails at its main job and ends the habit. Nobody has published a measurement of mic drain (vendor claims run 3 to 20 %/h), so the app has to measure and report what it finds. A watch recording on a desk or charger captures a room with no wearer present.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Set WKInterfaceDevice.current().isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true and sample batteryLevel and batteryState at each rotation.
    • Estimate %/h by linear regression over a window of at least 30 minutes. Verify how coarsely watchOS reports batteryLevel.
    • Free space: FileManager volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey. Verify it on watchOS; fall back to volumeAvailableCapacityKey. Purge acknowledged segments first.
    • Watch ProcessInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled and NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChange, and switch to 24 kbps in Low Power Mode. Recording under Low Power Mode is untested. Double Tap is unavailable there, so on-screen buttons remain.
    • Off-wrist: if batteryState changes to .charging, end the Session with a GAP (reason off_wrist_charging). Device test: take the watch off, let it lock, and check that writes continue (completeUnlessOpen) or stop cleanly. If watchOS exposes a lock or protected-data signal, treat it as off-wrist and prompt the user [verify].
    • At a limit: finalise the segment, call setActive(false), cancel the dead-man notification, and send a notification and haptic.
    • Log drain per watch model to opt-in telemetry.

  8. Status on the wrist: recording screen as watch face, complication and Smart Stack

    During a Session, watchOS shows the app on every wrist raise, so the recording screen is designed as a stand-in for the watch face. It shows the current time large, and the state and elapsed time smaller. The complication and Smart Stack show the current state and today's coverage and gaps. States: REC, Paused until hh:mm, Resume?, Resume needed, Queued n, Waiting for iPhone, Transcribed through hh:mm, about X hours left, and Check recording when the app has stopped confirming.

    Why it's inIt answers 'is it still recording, and did it work?' without opening the phone. It also keeps the watch useful as a watch while the app occupies the screen for hours.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • Recording screen: the time uses TimelineView(.everyMinute); the state chip and elapsed time use Text(timerInterval:). The next calendar event is optional.
    • Always-on: a reduced-luminance variant using the isLuminanceReduced environment value. No waveform or animation.
    • Verify on device whether the user can return to their watch face during a background audio session and whether the 'Return to Clock' setting applies. Measure the screen cost per raise and include it in the battery gate.
    • Complication and Smart Stack widgets read an App Group store.
    • Reload timelines only on state changes, plus the 15-minute push of the dead-man entry. Elapsed time needs no reloads.
    • iPhone processing status arrives through updateApplicationContext.

  9. Moment bookmark (Double Tap)

    Cut first if time is short

    While recording, Double Tap (or a tap on the Bookmark button) flags the last ~60 seconds, confirmed with a click haptic. The phone pins that span and gives it more weight in summaries and action items. It marks what to remember. It cannot answer 'what did they just say', because transcripts take minutes.

    Why it's inIt adds intent to ambient capture at almost no cost on the watch. It is not essential to a recorder that works, so it is the first thing cut if the phone-side weighting is not ready.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • On the recording screen, the Bookmark button carries .handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction).
    • watchOS brings the app forward on wrist raise during a background audio session, so a bookmark is a raise plus a pinch. Verify on device that Double Tap reliably brings the app forward.
    • Write {timestamp, lookback: 60} into the open segment's sidecar and play WKInterfaceDevice play(.click). The ring buffer and existing segments already hold the audio.
    • Decision: the bookmark, not Pause (Proposal 3), owns Double Tap on this screen. A false trigger costs nothing.
    • Avoid the Crown double-press.

  10. Evening recap on the wrist

    Cut first if time is short

    After the phone has processed the day, the Smart Stack and complication add up to 3 commitments or decisions with due dates. If the day has not been processed, the recap says 'Not processed yet - open iPhone' instead of showing nothing. It is read-only.

    Why it's inIt closes the habit loop where the habit lives, but it depends on the iPhone transcribing and summarising in time. Transcription may wait for charging, so the recap ships only when that pipeline is reliable.

    How to build it on watchOS
    • The iPhone sends a compact payload: state, coverage, gap count, and up to 3 items with due dates and span IDs.
    • Use transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo when a complication is on the active face. It has a daily budget: check remainingComplicationUserInfoTransfers. Whether it works with WidgetKit complications is [M]. Otherwise use transferUserInfo.
    • The watch saves the payload to the App Group store and reloads WidgetKit timelines.
    • RelevanceKit raises the Start widget in the morning and the recap in the evening.
    • No transcripts, chat or editing on the watch. 'Send to Reminders' runs on the iPhone.

Left out of the minimal app on purpose

  • Automatic, voice-triggered or scheduled start; automatic resume after interruptionsNot possible: capture must start from a user action in the foreground and cannot resume from the background [H]. It is also the weakest legal position. Schedules and context only prompt the user to tap.
  • Auto-resume after Pause as the defaultIt could quietly start recording again someone who asked not to be recorded. Resuming needs the wearer's tap. Auto-resume is an opt-in setting and is never offered in strict jurisdictions.
  • HKWorkoutSession or WKExtendedRuntimeSession as a keep-aliveDevelopers report repeated rejections (guideline 2.5.4/2.5.1). A workout session also moves Activity rings and drains power, and extended sessions are capped at 10 minutes to 1 hour with one type per app.
  • Recording while charging or off the wristIt captures a room with no wearer present, which no bystander-consent reasoning covers. Charging ends the Session.
  • Transcription, live captions or a live transcript on the watchwatchOS has no SFSpeechRecognizer or SpeechAnalyzer [H]. System dictation returns final text only and stops after about 30-45 seconds. Streaming to the phone for captions would need sockets, which are restricted.
  • LLM summaries on the watch, or features that depend on PCCThe watch has no on-device model. PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel needs a managed entitlement, works online only and hits daily quotas (quotaLimitReached).
  • A Live Rewind clone on the Digital CrownApple owns the Crown double-press on Series 12 and Ultra 4. Without speech recognition on the watch, a phone round trip would take minutes and feel broken. The bookmark covers 'remember that', not 'what did they just say'.
  • Real-time WebSocket or socket streaming to the cloud or a MacTN3135 restricts low-level networking. The network path has been measured dropping every ~36-38 s during audio sessions (FB24377808), and a watch app cannot reach a Mac over Bonjour or raw TCP.
  • Hidden or 'discreet' mode, or a Session with no start cueThe orange indicator cannot be hidden, and guidelines 2.5.14 and 2.5.19 and the EDPB forbid it. On a device that looks covert, it would invite wiretap claims. Users may choose a softer chime, but never remove the haptic, the screen state or the consent reminder.
  • Ask or chat on the wrist in v1The watch has no LLM, sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is in the background, and Petey's 3.8 rating shows chat on the wrist is hard. Moved to Later.
  • Transcript browsing, search or editing on the watchThe screen is too small and it costs battery. The phone owns review; the watch shows at most 3 read-only items.
  • Proactive nudges beyond the resume, pause-ended, guard-stop and sync notificationsFriend 2.0's unprompted texts and Omi's 'micromanager' reputation show the backlash, and nudges cost battery. Commitment nudges come later, gated on the phone.
  • Naming other speakers or storing bystander voiceprintsThese may count as GDPR Art. 9 biometric data, and they break social trust. The minimal app separates only 'me' from 'others', on the phone, using the wearer's own enrolled voice.
  • Actions run from the wrist (send email, post to Slack, create events)A tiny approval screen with a large potential for damage. Routing to the user's own tools is approved on the iPhone; outbound messaging is Later.
  • Phone-call captureCalls interrupt watch capture anyway, and they are the most regulated recording context. It belongs on the iPhone later, with an announcement that can't be turned off.
  • Session mode in the EEA, UK or Germany at launchThe EDPB statement, the criminal exposure under §201 StGB and Limitless's withdrawal from the EU and UK show the risk. Memo ships first; Sessions follow after a DPIA.
  • Third-party cloud AI on by default, or Message Batches and message threads under the zero-retention promiseGuideline 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission, and the Otter suit alleges training on recordings. Message threads are not ZDR-eligible, and ZDR eligibility for Batches is unconfirmed. The app is fully useful with on-device processing on the iPhone.
  • Keeping raw audio by default beyond 72 hours, or past transcription for strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consentIt adds legal and breach exposure, and the EDPB recommends persistent storage off by default. A short verification window where consent allows it, plus transcripts, gives most of the trust benefit.
  • Opus or LPCM recording; .m4a as the primary segment containerOpus encoding on the watch is unverified, and LPCM is about 115 MB per hour. An MP4 container can't be read until it is closed, so it loses the open segment in a crash. AAC mono at 24-32 kbps in ADTS takes about 10.8-14.4 MB per hour.
  • Depending on AudioRecordingIntent or a Live Activity on the watchThe docs require a Live Activity, but Activity.request lists only iOS and macOS, so behaviour on the watch is unclear [L]. The system indicator and the in-app state are enough for now; test later.
  • MCP or desktop agent access in v1An iPhone app can't host a local MCP server for desktop agents. MCP comes in v1.x, served by a minimal signed Mac reader over the exported files.
  • Wrist-flick or pinch triggers, health or location fusion, translation, sharing linksWrist flick and pinch have no developer API. The rest collect more data or add leak risk without adding capture value.
  • Live waveform or animation on the always-on display during captureIt uses battery while the wrist is down and tells the user nothing. A static screen built around the time of day carries what matters.

How it fits together

Capture

The watch is a thin, honest recorder.

Start and activation:

  • Each Session is a series of capture runs. A run is started by Start or by a user Resume, always in the foreground.
  • Activate AVAudioSession once per run, never during silence or Pause, and keep an AVAudioEngine input tap running in the 'audio' background mode with the wrist down.
  • Each Resume is a new run, so test URLSession and CloudKit after resumes (FB24377808).

Category and routing:

  • .record by default. .playAndRecord only if the chime and Announce pass the device test.
  • No .allowBluetooth (HFP) option, so input stays on the watch mic.
  • Any input-route change writes a GAP. If input leaves the built-in mic, the run ends with a resume prompt.

The engine never stops automatically. Silence and paused audio are dropped in RAM before the encoder. The mic is released only by Stop, Discard of the whole Session, a guard stop, or charging.

Pipeline:

  • A ring buffer of at least 4 s.
  • An energy gate; the 2 s pre-roll is taken from the moment it trips.
  • SoundAnalysis speech confirmation, then a 3 s hangover.
  • AAC-LC mono 16 kHz at 32 kbps (24 kbps in Low Power Mode), written as ADTS in 2-minute segments.
  • JSON sidecars and an fsync'd journal.
  • Files are created with completeUnlessOpen protection.
  • If watchOS cannot write ADTS, segments become 60 s .m4a files and the app states that a crash can lose up to a minute.

Rotation runs on wall-clock time and doubles as a heartbeat: each rotation reschedules a 5-minute dead-man notification and keeps the complication's 'last confirmed' entry fresh.

Interruptions (AVAudioSession interruption and route change, media reset, engine configuration change):

  1. Post the resume notification first.
  2. Close the segment and write a GAP.
  3. Show Resume on the complication.

Charging ends the Session as an off-wrist proxy.

Not used:

  • HKWorkoutSession or extended-runtime keep-alives (guideline 2.5.4; the Earshot notes cite 2.5.1; the outcome is the same).
  • The Crown double-press.
  • AudioRecordingIntent or a Live Activity.

Devices:

  • Target watchOS 27: Series 9 and later, Ultra 2 and later, SE 3.
  • A watchOS 26 fallback [M] reaches Series 6-8, SE 2 and Ultra 1, without Double Tap. It ships only after soak tests on those models.

Conflict noted: sources disagree on whether Granola keeps recording when the user checks a text. Apple's engineer confirms that background recording continues. I therefore assume that viewing other apps that don't use audio keeps capture running, and that anything taking the audio session (dictation, timers with sound, Siri) interrupts it. Nothing is marketed until this is verified on a device.

Transcription and AI

The watch runs nothing except voice-activity detection: no Speech framework, no SystemLanguageModel, and PCC has quotas and needs a managed entitlement.

iPhone (required)

When processing happens:

  • A WatchConnectivity wake only verifies, stores and acknowledges a segment.
  • Transcription runs when the app is opened, in a BGProcessingTask that requires external power (usually overnight), and from a 'Process now' button. The button starts a user-initiated BGContinuedProcessingTask on iOS 26 [M: verify that long SpeechAnalyzer jobs fit].
  • Until then the watch shows 'Waiting for iPhone'.

Transcription:

  • SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber for timestamped long-form transcripts. It has no custom vocabulary and handles only a few languages at a time; check availability per iPhone model.
  • WhisperKit as the fallback (verify on iOS).

Wearer vs others:

  • About 30 s of the wearer's own voice is enrolled at onboarding.
  • Each speech turn gets a speaker embedding from a Core ML model, scored against the wearer's embedding. Candidates: a WeSpeaker- or ECAPA-class model converted to Core ML, or FluidAudio's iOS build with pyannote community-1 [verify].
  • This is combined with a wrist-proximity cue: the wearer's voice is louder relative to the noise floor.
  • Acceptance gate before it drives retention: wearer-attribution precision of at least 95% at a fixed confidence threshold, on labelled real wrist audio across watch models, wrist positions and rooms.
  • Turns below the threshold are 'uncertain' and treated as others.
  • Until the gate passes, strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consent keep only summaries of what others said.

Media and sensitive content:

  • SoundAnalysis plus ShazamKit drop TV and music.
  • Sensitive-content filters run on transcripts and derived objects before they are saved and before anything leaves the device. The audio of a flagged span is shredded immediately.
  • Tombstones from Discard are applied before every step.

Summaries:

  • Apple Foundation Models on iPhones with Apple Intelligence. The session context is 4,096 tokens, so the app triages each segment with @Generable schemas and then rolls up.
  • Every derived object carries source_span_ids, and a coverage table backs 'not recorded' answers.
  • iPhones without Apple Intelligence still get transcripts; summaries there need the cloud opt-in.

Decision: the iPhone, not the Mac (as in the Earshot notes), is the default node. Requiring a Mac shrinks the market, and SpeechAnalyzer runs on iOS 26. Full diarization on the Mac comes with the Later companion.

Cloud tier (v1.x)

Opt-in per provider, through one logged, redacting exit point, and nothing younger than 15 minutes leaves the device.

Models:

  • claude-haiku-5-5 for per-conversation extraction: $0.10/$0.50 per MTok up to 100K-token prompts, $0.50/$2.50 above.
  • claude-opus-5-5 for nightly synthesis: $4/$20 per MTok. Set output_config.effort explicitly; the default is medium, and thinking cannot be disabled.

Request rules:

  • Structured outputs through output_config.format, or strict tools with tool_choice auto. Forced any/tool returns 400.
  • No temperature, top_p or top_k on API 2026-10-21, and no prefill.
  • Check stop_reason 'refusal' and stop_details.

Refusal fallbacks:

  • Opus 5.5: enable server-side fallbacks (beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01). Use the array form naming a model your ZDR arrangement covers rather than 'default', and confirm with Anthropic that the target stays within ZDR.
  • Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback, so its refusals are handled in the client.

Zero retention:

  • Requires a ZDR arrangement on the vendor's Anthropic organization; the Messages API is ZDR-eligible.
  • Message Batches (50% off) are used only after Anthropic confirms that Batches qualify under ZDR. Until then, nightly synthesis runs as standard Messages requests at full price.
  • Message threads are not ZDR-eligible and are not used.

Keys:

  • iPhone calls use App Attest through ClaudeForFoundationModels (beta; no batch, MCP connector or prompt-caching control).
  • Any proxy is stateless and logs metadata only, never payloads.
  • Users who bring their own key see a notice that their provider's retention terms apply.

Model IDs, prices and request rules were checked against the Claude API reference (cached Nov 3, 2026).

Sync and storage

Watch to iPhone:

  • WCSession.transferFile for each closed segment, with {session, seq, sha256}.
  • The iPhone verifies the hash, writes the segment durably and acknowledges through transferUserInfo, not sendMessage.
  • The watch deletes a segment only after an acknowledgement, re-queues failed or stale outstandingFileTransfers, and holds nothing else.

When the iPhone is unreachable:

  • After 15 minutes with no acknowledgement, the watch saves the segment as a CKAsset to the user's CloudKit private database with CKModifyRecordsOperation, during the recording session's runtime. This follows DTS's advice in forum 843751 to use runtime the app already has. I chose it over the Earshot notes' 'always background'.
  • A successful save counts as the receipt. Leftovers retry in background refresh tasks.
  • The iPhone imports through a database subscription, de-duplicates by (session, seq, sha256) against the WatchConnectivity path, and deletes the CloudKit record after import.
  • There is no vendor endpoint.

Discard tombstones:

  • Travel by transferUserInfo and stay in the watch journal until acknowledged.
  • Also delete any CloudKit copy.

No sockets (TN3135; path revocation FB24377808). Expect minutes of latency. Test with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off; transferFile does not work in the Simulator.

Back to the watch:

  • Status through updateApplicationContext.
  • The recap through transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo when a complication is on the active face (daily budget; check remainingComplicationUserInfoTransfers), otherwise transferUserInfo.
  • Everything lands in an App Group store that the complications and Smart Stack read.

iPhone vault:

  • Encrypted SQLite, a documented JSON schema, a Markdown mirror, and audio stored as ADTS (transcoded to .m4a on export).

Retention:

  • In strict jurisdictions without logged consent, audio is shredded when transcription succeeds.
  • Otherwise audio is kept 72 hours by default (0 hours to 30 days, or pinned), then crypto-shredded.
  • Flagged spans and discarded ranges are shredded immediately.
  • The wearer's transcript is kept until the user deletes it.
  • Retention keys are set per tier, day and consent state.

Exit guarantee:

  • A scheduled and on-demand export of the schema, Markdown and audio (within its retention) to Files or iCloud Drive, parsed by a published open-source reader.
  • CloudKit private-database sync (encryptedValues) is only a convenience, because only apps signed by the owning team can read a CloudKit container.
  • In v1.x, a minimal signed Mac reader reads the export folder and serves the local read-only MCP.

Sizes:

  • 10.8-14.4 MB per hour of speech at 24-32 kbps; ADTS headers add about 0.4 MB/h.
  • A fully ungated 16-hour day is about 175-230 MB, against roughly 64 GB of storage.
  • Segments are 2 minutes (the brief says 1-5 minutes, the Earshot notes 2), about 0.5 MB each. That is far below the size of the reported failing file, which was under 30 MB.
Battery budget

No rigorous public measurement exists, so every figure here is an estimate until measured.

What is known:

  • Rated life covers all use: Series 11/12 24 h, SE 3 18 h, Ultra 3 42 h, Ultra 4 50 h.
  • Research estimate [L] for recording from 100% to a 10-15% stop: Series 11/12 about 10-14 h, SE 3 about 8-11 h, Ultra 3 about 18-24 h.
  • Vendor claims run from about 3 %/h (Hedy) to 15-20 %/h.

Ship gates measure total drain while recording during a scripted day with realistic wrist raises and notifications. The scripted day matters because the recording screen appears on every raise.

  • Series 11/12: 7 %/h or less, about 12 h from 100% to the 15% stop. Stretch goal 6 %/h, about 14 h. A 07:00-19:00 day ends near 16% at 7 %/h and near 28% at 6 %/h.
  • SE 3: the same power draw is roughly 9 %/h on its smaller battery, about 9 h. Claim 'most of a workday' or 'your meetings', not 'a workday'.
  • Ultra 3/4: roughly 3.5-4 %/h, about 21-25 h. Claim 'a full waking day'.
  • Series 6-8, SE 2 and Ultra 1 on the watchOS 26 fallback: batteries are aging, so no claim until soak-tested.

Power plan:

  • The mic and encoder run continuously.
  • SoundAnalysis runs only when the energy gate trips.
  • The radio wakes in short batches.
  • Widgets reload only on state changes, plus once every 15 minutes for the dead-man entry.
  • No animation while the wrist is down, no PCC calls, no streaming.
  • Voice gating saves encoder, storage and radio power, not mic power.
  • Measure the screen cost per wrist raise and include it in the gate.

Guards: stop at 15% battery, under 100 MB free, or on charging. Drop to 24 kbps in Low Power Mode; recording under Low Power Mode is untested.

Measurement: drain is a regression over at least 30 minutes of batteryLevel samples, showing 'Measuring...' until then. Verify how coarsely watchOS reports batteryLevel. Log drain per model to opt-in telemetry.

Publish no battery number until it is measured on Series 9 and later, SE 3 and Ultra.

Inputs and UI

Entry points:

  • a complication
  • a Smart Stack widget
  • a watchOS 26 Control (Control Center, Smart Stack, or the Ultra Action Button through the Control)
  • Double Tap inside the app

Controls and widgets open the app, because capture must start in the foreground.

Start screen preflight row: mic, notifications and Time Sensitive, companion app, storage, and battery against projected hours.

  • A missing mic permission or companion app blocks Start.
  • Denied notifications show 'Interruptions won't alert you', which the user must acknowledge before starting.
  • In the EEA, UK and Germany the screen offers Memo only.

Double Tap (.handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction)) does one thing per screen:

  • Start screen: Start.
  • Recording screen: Bookmark, if it ships.
  • Paused, pause-ended and Interrupted screens: Resume.

It needs S9 or later, the wrist raised and Low Power Mode off, so on-screen buttons always exist. Double Tap never discards or stops.

Recording screen:

  • watchOS brings the app back on every raise during a background audio session, so this screen stands in for the watch face.
  • The current time is large; the state (REC or Paused) and elapsed time (Text(timerInterval:)) are secondary. The next calendar event is optional.
  • A reduced-luminance variant for always-on. No waveform.
  • Pause is the largest button. Stop and Discard are secondary. Discard offers last 5 min, last 15 min or this Session, takes two taps and has a 5-second undo.
  • Memo is press-and-hold on the main button.
  • Verify on device whether the user can return to their face and whether 'Return to Clock' applies.

Complication and Smart Stack states: REC with elapsed time; Paused (until hh:mm); Resume?; Resume needed; Queued n; Waiting for iPhone; Transcribed through hh:mm; about X h left; and a pre-scheduled 'Check recording - last confirmed hh:mm' for when the app stops confirming.

The Smart Stack recap, if shipped, shows coverage, gaps and up to 3 items. RelevanceKit raises Start in the morning and the recap in the evening.

Not on the watch: transcripts, chat or editing. The Crown double-press is left to Apple's Live Rewind. Wrist flick and the single pinch have no developer API.

Notifications in v1:

  • resume, including the dead-man notification
  • the pause-ended prompt
  • guard stops
  • sync errors
Privacy and consent

Capture:

  • Only the user starts capture. There is no voice-triggered or hidden recording, and copy avoids 'always listening'.
  • Putting the watch on the charger ends the Session.

Start cue:

  • The orange indicator cannot be hidden.
  • A Session always starts with a haptic, the full-screen state and the consent reminder.
  • An audible chime is added only if a device test shows it plays in Silent Mode and on the built-in speaker with AirPods connected.
  • Users may choose a softer tone but not silence. Granola users complain its chime cannot be disabled.
  • Memos may be haptic-only.

Consent reminder and jurisdiction:

  • The reminder appears at every Session start, everywhere.
  • Jurisdiction comes from coarse location at each Session start. The onboarding answer is the fallback, and an unknown location is treated as strict.
  • Jurisdiction sets only the retention and Announce defaults.
  • Strict set: Kilpatrick's 13 all-party-consent states (CA, CT, DE, FL, IL, MD, MA, MT, NV, NH, OR, PA, WA) plus Michigan, a hybrid in the brief. The brief says 11-13 states; I chose the conservative list plus MI.

Announce:

  • An on-screen script for the wearer to say aloud.
  • A pre-recorded notice plays only when the audio output route is the built-in speaker; otherwise the card says 'Tell people you're recording'.
  • Logged as announced_by: speaker, wearer_confirmed or none.
  • An 'Everyone agreed' confirmation covers audio from that moment on, never earlier audio.

Pause and Discard:

  • Pause asks before resuming. Auto-resume is opt-in and never offered in strict jurisdictions. An unanswered pause becomes Stop after 10 minutes.
  • Discard (last 5 or 15 minutes, or the Session) applies on the watch, and by tombstone on the iPhone, before transcription and before any cloud use. The exit point holds everything for 15 minutes.

Retention:

  • Audio is necessarily stored briefly before transcription: encrypted on the watch until acknowledged, then in the iPhone vault.
  • Strict jurisdiction without logged consent:
    • Audio is shredded as soon as transcription succeeds, and pinning is off.
    • Other people's words are summarised without quotes, and their transcript text is deleted once the summary exists.
    • If wearer separation is below its gate, everything said by others in that session is kept as summary only.
  • Elsewhere, or with consent: audio is kept 72 hours by default (0 hours to 30 days, or pinned), then crypto-shredded.
  • The wearer's transcript is kept until the user deletes it.
  • Sensitive filters (IDs, payment, logins, health, self-harm) run on transcripts and derived objects before they are saved and before anything leaves the device. The audio of a flagged span is shredded immediately.
  • Deleting by time range or session also serves bystander requests.
  • These rules limit retention exposure but do not cure interception claims, so the start-of-Session notice remains the main control.

Other defaults:

  • Session mode is 18+. Decision: Apple's own Siri Recap support doc says 18+; I followed it over the Earshot notes' secondary 'not for under-13s'.
  • Pause zones and Focus links come as a Differentiator.
  • Third-party AI:
    • opt-in per provider, redacted, through one logged exit point;
    • zero-retention claims only for paths confirmed as ZDR (no Batches until confirmed, no message threads);
    • any proxy is stateless;
    • bring-your-own-key users see a notice.
  • No vendor copy by default. The exit guarantee is exported files plus an open-source reader.
  • EEA, UK and Germany: Memo only at launch; Session mode waits for a DPIA.
  • Ship through TestFlight first and book Meet with Apple before App Store submission.

Your build

The minimal set against Earshot

Earshot, the always-listening Watch recorder in this repository (PR #3), already does a lot. Checked against its watch code: 3 of the 10 minimal items are built, 6 are partly there and 1 is missing.

Minimal itemEarshotWhat it does todayWhat to change
One-tap foreground start, preflight, consent reminder and start cue ◐Partly One tap starts all-day capture, but only from inside the app. There are no complications, Smart Stack widget or Control yet (README lists this as a gap). No preflight check for notification permission or a reachable companion, no per-session consent reminder, and no start chime in the watch code. Add a WidgetKit complication and a watchOS 26 Control that open the app to Start, a preflight row (mic, Time Sensitive notifications, Mac or iPhone reachable, storage, battery), and a 2-second consent card with a haptic cue.
Speech-gated capture into segments that survive a crash ◐Partly Writes 2-minute 16 kHz AAC segments and measures how much of each is speech; near-silent segments are skipped. Segments are .m4a files through AVAudioFile, and SegmentQueue discards an unreadable file after a crash ("recording was cut off"), so the open segment is lost. Silence is skipped per segment, not per utterance. Write ADTS (.aac) so a crash loses at most one frame, gate the encoder on speech with a pre-roll ring buffer, and set file protection on segment files.
Delivery ledger with receipts and visible states ●Built Segments wait in an on-disk queue and are deleted only after the Mac acknowledges them; the watch shows the queued count and last sync. Uploads go straight to the Mac over a foreground URLSession. Keep the ledger. Test the direct-to-Mac path during long sessions: the research found a report of the network path dropping every 36-38 s during audio sessions (single source, check on device). WatchConnectivity to an iPhone relay is the fallback the research recommends.
Interruption handling, dead-man's switch and one-tap resume ◐Partly Calls and Siri close the segment with a reason and post "Earshot isn't recording" with a resume action; recording resumes when the app is opened. Nothing fires if the app is killed or crashes without seeing an interruption. Reschedule a 5-minute local notification at every segment rotation so a silent death still alerts the wearer, and pre-schedule a "Check recording" complication entry.
Timed Pause that asks before resuming, and Stop ◐Partly Privacy pause for 15 minutes, 1 hour or until resumed; it turns the mic off. When a timed pause ends, recording restarts by itself if the app is on screen, otherwise a notification asks the wearer to tap. Ask before resuming every time (no automatic restart), and turn an unanswered prompt into Stop after 10 minutes.
Discard the last 5 minutes, last 15 minutes or the whole session ○Missing No discard control. Raw audio is deleted on the Mac after 7 days by default (0 deletes it after transcription), but a bystander's request can't be honoured on the spot. Add a two-tap Discard with a 5-second undo that deletes unsent audio on the watch and sends a tombstone the Mac applies before transcription.
Battery, storage and off-wrist guards ◐Partly Shows a battery forecast measured from real drain, stops at 10% battery, and keeps a 100 MB free-space reserve for the queue. Charging only pauses the forecast; recording continues on the charger. End the session when the watch starts charging (an off-wrist proxy), and consider stopping at 15% so the watch still works as a watch.
Status on the wrist: recording screen, complication and Smart Stack ◐Partly The Record and Today views show state, words and minutes recorded, queue and battery forecast. There is no complication or Smart Stack widget, so status needs the app open. Design the recording screen as a stand-in watch face (large time, small state), and add a complication with REC, Paused, Resume needed and Queued states.
Moment bookmark on Double Tap (cut first) ●Built A Mark button and Double Tap bookmark the moment, and bookmarked moments are weighted in analysis. None needed.
Evening recap on the wrist (cut first) ●Built A daily digest is generated on the Mac after 21:00 and a notice goes to the watch, plus a weekly review on Sundays. None needed for the minimal set. A Smart Stack card would show it without a notification.

Where Earshot and the recommendation part ways

  • Earshot already goes well past the minimal set: Ask, Do and Note from the wrist, proactive questions, a Mac agent with computer use, goals and a memory MCP server. The recommendation puts wrist Ask and outbound actions in Later, and keeps nudges to at most 2 a day by default (Earshot allows 6).
  • Earshot processes everything on the Mac. The recommendation makes the iPhone the default processing node so the app works without a Mac, and keeps the Mac for heavier diarization, meeting capture and MCP later.
  • Earshot is built for personal installs from Xcode and its README expects App Review to reject it. The recommendation is written for an App Store build, which is why it insists on user-started sessions, visible cues and no keep-alive tricks.

Earshot watch app on branch claude/beautiful-hypatia-m7ctpu (PR #3), commit e36b1b5, 14 Nov 2026: earshot/Watch/*.swift, README.md and docs/FEATURES.md.

Recommendation 2

The best overall feature set

For a full product across Watch, iPhone and, later, the Mac. Core features carry a release stage: v1 ships first, v1.x follows.

Core

Table stakes. Users expect these on day one.

16 features

One-tap capture the user starts (Session and Memo), behind a preflight check

v1

A Session starts with one tap from any of: a complication, a Smart Stack widget, a watchOS 26 Control (Control Center, Smart Stack or the Ultra Action Button), or Double Tap on the Start screen. A preflight check runs first: microphone and notification permission, Time Sensitive alerts, companion app installed, free storage, and battery against projected hours. The Session then records in the background with the wrist down and can be time-boxed ('until 6 pm'). A Memo is press-and-hold on the in-app button to capture a thought; it uses the same pipeline and is tagged as a note. Schedules only remind the user to tap. In the EEA, UK and Germany only Memo ships at launch. Copy says 'Session', never 'always listening'.

Seen inWhisper MemosJust Press RecordGranolaCirclebackPlaud NotePin SPebble Index 01

Why

A foreground start by the user is the only legitimate way to record for hours on watchOS [H]. It is also the strongest position for App Review and consent law. One-tap start is the most-praised trait of watch recorders. The preflight exists because the honest-gap design (resume nudges, dead-man notification) fails silently if notification permission or the companion app is missing. Decision: I adopted Proposal 3's Memo/Session split because quick capture is the top watch use case, and implemented both on one pipeline (Proposal 1) so the Memo adds no new mechanism.

Capture pipeline that never silently loses audio, with visible sync states

v1

Speech is written in 2-minute ADTS (.aac) segments, encrypted at rest with file protection, and recorded in a hashed journal. A segment is deleted from the watch only after the iPhone confirms receipt, or after a successful save to the user's CloudKit private database. ADTS frames are self-delimiting, so a crash loses at most the last partial frame. If ADTS writing proves unsupported on watchOS, segments drop to 60-second .m4a files and the app says plainly that a crash can lose up to a minute. The watch and phone show each segment's state: Recorded, Queued, On iPhone, Waiting for iPhone, Transcribed.

Seen inGranolaBluedotHiDock P1Fieldy 3 (formerly Compass)Omi (open-source platform & SDK)

Why

Lost or never-transferred recordings are the top complaint: Omi lost an 11-hour watch recording, Voice Memos truncated an hour to seconds, and Drafts sync broke after a watchOS update. One silent loss destroys trust. Granola's sync states with retry are the reference design. Decision: ADTS rather than .m4a, because an MP4 container cannot be read until its moov atom is written at close. 'Recoverable after a crash' is true only for a crash-tolerant format.

Interruption handling that records the gap honestly, with a dead-man's switch

v1

When a call, Siri, an alarm or another audio app ends capture, the app first posts a time-sensitive 'Recording stopped - tap to resume'. It then closes the segment, records a GAP with the reason, and shows Resume on the complication. A crash, jetsam or the end of background runtime sends no notification, so every 2-minute segment rotation also reschedules a local notification for 5 minutes later. If rotations stop for any reason, that notification fires. The complication also pre-schedules a 'Check recording - last confirmed hh:mm' state, which the running app keeps pushing forward. Summaries and answers are told about every gap and never fill one in.

Seen inGranolaVoicenotesApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

Why

Capture cannot be resumed from the background (Apple Frameworks Engineer, forum 750432), and recordings that stop on interruption are the second most common complaint. A stop the app never observes is the worst case, because the user believes the whole day is being recorded. Crash recovery at next launch repairs files but tells nobody. A gap the user was told about is forgivable; one discovered later is not.

Clear recording state, a consent reminder at every Session, and Announce

v1

Recording is shown by:

  • the system orange mic indicator;
  • a start cue: a haptic, plus a short chime on the built-in speaker if the chime passes a device test;
  • a full-screen recording state;
  • a REC complication.

Every Session, everywhere, opens with a 2-second consent reminder. Jurisdiction comes from coarse location at each Session start and is treated as strict when unknown. It sets only the retention and Announce defaults. In the 14 strict US states (Kilpatrick's 13 plus Michigan), Announce is pre-selected.

Announce is an on-screen script for the wearer to say aloud. A pre-recorded notice also plays, but only when audio output is the built-in speaker. Each session log records:

  • whether the user was reminded;
  • announced_by: speaker, wearer_confirmed or none;
  • any 'Everyone agreed' confirmation, which covers audio from that moment on, never earlier audio.

In the EEA, UK and Germany only Memo ships at launch. These Session rules apply there once the DPIA-gated Later item ships.

Seen inGranolaApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)viaim RecDotFlowtica VersoPixel Call NotesTruecaller AI Call Recording

Why

Guideline 2.5.14 requires explicit consent and a clear indication of recording. The EDPB says consent obtained after recording is invalid and that indicators should be hard to disable. A watch looks covert to bystanders. The reminder appears everywhere because users travel and calls cross state lines, where the strictest rule generally applies; it costs almost nothing. Decision: no claim that the chime 'cannot be turned off' until it is shown on hardware to play in Silent Mode and on the built-in speaker with AirPods connected. Users may pick a softer tone, since Granola users complain its chime cannot be disabled, but a Session never starts without a cue the wearer can see and feel.

Timed Pause that asks before resuming, and Stop that turns the mic off

v1

Pause lasts 15 minutes by default (1 hour optional) and keeps nothing. When the timer ends, the watch taps the wrist and asks 'Resume recording?'. If nobody answers within 10 minutes, the Pause becomes a Stop. Auto-resume is an opt-in setting and is never available in strict jurisdictions. Stop turns the mic off and the orange indicator goes out. The screen always states which mode is active, for example 'Paused - mic open, nothing saved'.

Seen inFellowSlack AI huddle notesLimitless PendantApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

Why

People drop these devices first in social settings: a long-term Limitless user stopped wearing it socially, and a Bee user's partner banned it at home. Decision: this merges Proposal 1's soft pause (only a pause that keeps the audio session alive can resume without re-activation), Proposal 2's real mic-off (Stop), and Proposal 3's time limit. An automatic resume could quietly start recording again someone who asked not to be recorded, so resuming needs the wearer's tap. The conversion to Stop keeps the mic from staying open indefinitely with nothing kept.

Discard what was just recorded

v1

The recording screen and the complication offer 'Discard last 5 min / last 15 min / this Session'. Discarding takes two taps, has a 5-second undo, and is never mapped to Double Tap. The watch deletes matching unsent audio and sends a tombstone. The iPhone applies the tombstone before transcription or any cloud use, deleting audio, transcript spans, derived objects and search entries in that range. Nothing leaves the device until a span is at least 15 minutes old, so a 15-minute discard always wins.

Seen inBubblesFellowSlack AI huddle notesLimitless Pendant

Why

Pause and Stop only prevent future capture. Consent obtained after recording is invalid (EDPB), and Limitless's own guidance says to delete audio captured without consent. When a bystander says 'please delete that', the wearer has to be able to do it on the spot, not later on the phone after the audio has been transcribed.

Verifiable record (full transcript, me vs others, cited summaries, short audio window)

v1, gated on a spike

A full timestamped transcript separates the enrolled wearer from everyone else. Every summary line, decision and action item links to the transcript span it came from. Where audio is kept, tapping a line plays the original audio during the verification window. In strict-jurisdiction Sessions without logged consent, no audio is kept, so citations point to text only. Uncertain speaker labels are marked as uncertain and treated as 'others' for retention. Wearer separation ships only after it passes an acceptance gate on real wrist audio: wearer-attribution precision of at least 95% at a fixed confidence threshold. Until then, strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consent keep only summaries of what others said.

Seen inPlaud Note ProTwinMindLegend OneAWS HealthScribeRev (AI Notetaker and Voice Recorder app)Whisper Notes

Why

Siri Recap gives summaries only, with no transcript or speakers. Bee deletes audio, so its TV-as-conversation errors and hallucinations cannot be checked. Accuracy failures hurt trust more than missing features do. Decision: me-vs-others stays Core (Proposals 1 and 3), not a Differentiator (Proposal 2), because strict-jurisdiction retention depends on it. It is labelled 'gated on a spike' because diarization has been verified only on the Mac (SpeakerKit needs macOS 14+). The iPhone candidate is a Core ML speaker-embedding model or a FluidAudio iOS build, combined with a wrist-proximity energy cue.

Search and Ask over history, with citations and 'not recorded' answers (phone)

v1 search, v1.x Ask

v1 adds full-text search on the iPhone (SQLite FTS). v1.x adds semantic search and plain-language questions. Every answer cites transcript spans, and a table of what was recorded lets it say 'not recorded' instead of guessing.

Seen inGranolaVoicenotesTwinMindPlaud NoteLimitless Pendant

Why

Finding things later is what justifies wearing a mic (ask AI about your history 112, searchable memory 111). A six-month Limitless user called it a 'fancy transcription service with a mediocre search', so answers must be cited and honest about gaps. Ask depends on the synthesis pipeline, so it follows in v1.x.

Action items and commitments sent to the user's own tools, with approval

v1 Reminders and Calendar, v1.x other tools

Extract to-dos, promises and dates. One tap on the iPhone sends an item to Reminders or Calendar (EventKit) in v1, and to Things, Todoist or Notion in v1.x. Nothing is created without approval.

Seen inPocketCleft NotesWhisper MemosPebble Index 01AI MindClipTodoist Ramble

Why

Action items are what people act on and pay for (135 of 272), and automatic routing is a favorite watch feature. Feeding the user's own task system needs no new habit. Decision: routing to the user's own tools is Core. Drafting or sending messages on the user's behalf waits for Later.

Retention set by jurisdiction, consent and the user

v1

Silence is never written. Audio must be stored briefly before anything can transcribe it: encrypted on the watch, then in the iPhone vault.

After transcription:

  • Strict jurisdiction without logged consent: audio is crypto-shredded as soon as transcription succeeds, and pinning is off.
  • Elsewhere, or once consent is logged: audio is kept 72 hours by default (the user can choose 0 hours to 30 days, or pin a session), then shredded.
  • The wearer's transcript is kept until the user deletes it.
  • In strict jurisdictions without logged consent, other people's words are summarised without quotes, and their transcript text is deleted once the summary is written.

Sensitive filters (IDs, payment, logins, health, self-harm) run on transcripts and derived objects before they are saved and before anything leaves the device. The audio of a flagged span is shredded immediately, not at the end of the window. The user can delete by time range or by session.

Seen inJumpFieldy 3 (formerly Compass)Raycon AI NotetakerTactiqZocksBee Frontier

Why

The earlier draft withheld unconsented bystanders' verbatim transcript but kept their raw audio for 72 hours, which is the more sensitive record. Filters cannot run on audio before it is stored, so they now apply to transcripts and trigger shredding of the matching audio. The EDPB recommends persistent storage off by default, Apple deletes Recap summaries after 7 days unless saved, and Jump already sells retention choices. Decision: where audio is kept, 72 hours (Proposal 3) rather than 7 days (Proposal 1). That covers the evening recap and the next morning's brief while shrinking breach and discovery exposure.

Third-party AI only after opt-in, through one logged exit point

v1 exit point, v1.x cloud tier

Cloud LLMs stay off until the user opts in to each provider. Names and numbers are redacted on the device. Every outbound call passes through one logged exit point, and nothing leaves the device until a span is 15 minutes old. The zero-retention promise covers only requests that really are zero-retention:

  • no Message Batches until Anthropic confirms they qualify;
  • no message threads, which are not ZDR-eligible.

The app ships no keys. iPhone calls use App Attest, and any proxy is stateless and logs no payloads. Users who bring their own API key are told that the provider's retention terms apply.

Seen inGrainJamieWillow VoiceClaude voice modeButton

Why

Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires naming third-party AI and getting explicit permission. Brewer v. Otter.ai alleges training on recordings. Grain advertises that it never trains on meeting data. A zero-retention claim is only as good as the weakest request path, so each path has to be confirmed rather than assumed.

Battery, storage and off-wrist guards with measured hours remaining

v1

The app measures drain on this watch over at least 30 minutes, showing 'Measuring...' until then, and then shows about how many hours are left. Capture stops cleanly at 15% battery, under 100 MB free, or when the watch starts charging (a proxy for being off the wrist). The bitrate drops in Low Power Mode. Claims are made per model:

  • Series 11/12: 'a workday Session', only once measured drain is 7 %/h or less.
  • SE 3: 'most of a workday'.
  • Ultra: 'a full waking day'.

Never '24/7'.

Seen inPebble Index 01TwinMindBee Eclipse

Why

Every battery figure in the category is a vendor claim, ranging from 3 to 20 %/h, and rated life covers all use. A watch that dies at 5 pm fails at being a watch and ends the habit. A watch left recording on a desk or charger captures a room with no wearer present, which no bystander-consent reasoning covers.

User-owned vault with an exit guarantee based on files

v1

An encrypted local-first vault on the iPhone: SQLite, a documented JSON schema, a Markdown mirror, and audio within its retention window. The exit guarantee is files: a scheduled export (weekly by default) and an on-demand export of the schema, Markdown and audio to Files or iCloud Drive. A published open-source reader can parse the export without an account. Optional multi-device sync uses the user's CloudKit private database (encryptedValues), so the vendor holds no copy. CloudKit is for sync only, not for leaving. Bulk export and one-tap delete-all are included.

Seen inOmi (open-source platform & SDK)Anarlog (formerly Hyprnote)Reflect (Reflect Open)Quill MeetingsScreenpipeWhisper Notes

Why

Limitless shut off capture and deleted regional data within two weeks of its acquisition, and Humane's devices were bricked. Missing bulk export is a recorded Voicenotes complaint. Decision: the guarantee rests on exported files because only apps signed by the team that owns a CloudKit container can read it. After a shutdown, a reader built from source by someone else could never reach CloudKit data.

Read-only agent access (MCP) through a minimal signed Mac reader

v1.x

A small, notarized Mac app reads the exported vault from iCloud Drive and serves a local read-only MCP server. Each client gets its own token, output is redacted, every request is logged, and broad queries need approval. It grows into the Later Mac companion.

Seen inGranolaPebble Index 01CirclebackQuill MeetingsScreenpipe

Why

Agent access is now expected: MCP ships in Granola, Omi, Pebble Index 01, Circleback, Otter.ai and Screenpipe. An iPhone app cannot host a local MCP server for desktop agents, so this needs a Mac. Decision: v1.x rather than v1 (Proposal 3 had MCP inside the vault item). That keeps v1 to the watch and iPhone, and the scope is stated in the summary. Reading the exported files keeps it independent of CloudKit.

Glanceable status and evening recap on the wrist

v1 status, recap only if the iPhone pipeline is ready

The recording screen, the complication and a Smart Stack widget show recording, sync and coverage state. The states include 'Waiting for iPhone' and a stale 'Check recording' warning. Once the phone has processed the day, they add the 1-3 commitments or decisions worth acting on. The recap ships in v1 only if the iPhone reliably processes the day; otherwise it is cut first. The wrist view is read-only and all detail stays on the phone.

Seen inTicNote WatchGranolaAI MindClipLegend OneApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)

Why

Status answers 'did it work?' where the habit lives, and it is essential. No third-party watch recorder shows the day's coverage and gaps on the wrist. The recap is the payoff (Siri Recap's best-received moment was a detail the family had forgotten), but it depends on the iPhone pipeline, which can lag until charging.

Moment bookmark

v1 if cheap, cut first

While recording, Double Tap flags the last ~60 seconds. The phone pins that span to the top of the day and gives it more weight in summaries and action items. A bookmark marks what to remember. It cannot answer 'what did they just say', because transcripts take minutes.

Seen inPlaud NotePin SSoundcore Work (AI Note Taker)Vocci AI Context RingFlowtica ScribeTicNote WatchBOYA Notra

Why

It is a cheap signal of what mattered in an ambient stream: a Limitless user judged only ~10% of 10 GB valuable. It is also the most repeated hardware affordance in the category. Decision: Double Tap goes to bookmarking, not Pause (Proposal 3). An accidental bookmark costs nothing, while an accidental pause silently loses audio. It is cut first because it depends on phone-side weighting.

Differentiator

Where a new product can beat the field.

7 features

Cover the users Apple leaves out

The primary target is Series 9-11, SE 3 and Ultra 2-3 on watchOS 27, which get no Siri Recap. A watchOS 26 fallback [M] reaches Series 6-8, SE 2 and Ultra 1. Those models get no Double Tap, so they use on-screen buttons only. They ship only after soak and battery tests, because their batteries are aging. iPhones without Apple Intelligence still get transcripts; check SpeechTranscriber availability per model. The product also offers more languages, records that last beyond Recap's 7 days, full transcripts and export. 'Keeps recording while you glance at other watch apps' is marketed only after a device test, because sources conflict on Granola: one says its recording stops when the user checks a text.

Seen inApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)TwinMindGranolaPlaud Note

Why

Siri Recap is limited to Series 12/Ultra 4 with an iPhone 16 or later, English only and outside the EU. Decision: 'older watches' means Series 9-11, SE 3 and Ultra 2-3 until the fallback models pass testing. The EU is not part of this differentiator (Proposals 1 and 2 listed it); Apple's absence there looks regulatory, so it moves to Later.

Consent Kit and bystander rights

Bystanders can open a consent card from a QR code or link shown on the iPhone; it shows what is kept and offers a deletion request. Templates help users notify a workplace. A consent log can be exported per session. Removing another person's words by time range needs no voiceprint.

Seen inviaim RecDotUphealBlueprintFellowAxon Draft One

Why

The EDPB says manufacturers cannot push GDPR duties onto users. No product in the catalog offers deletion aimed at the bystander. Social comfort is what keeps people using the product.

Start prompts from context, and pause zones

Calendar events, saved places and time windows trigger a haptic 'Start capture?' or a Smart Stack card. Places marked home, clinic, therapist or school, private calendar events and Focus modes prompt a pause.

Seen inGranolaApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)Vibe DotScreenpipeComulytic Note Pro

Why

Siri Recap can be scheduled by time or place, but third-party apps cannot start capture automatically [H]. A well-timed prompt is the honest equivalent, and pause zones protect social acceptability.

Commitment tracking with rare, gated nudges

Track promises by person and due date. Nudge only when a deadline is near or before meeting that person. Each nudge must name the decision it helps with, there are at most 2 a day by default, notifications are passive, and quiet hours apply.

Seen inLuna (Moon pendant) + SamanthaHalliday G2Comulytic Note ProFriend 2.0

Why

This is a high-value job and the whole pitch of Luna + Samantha. Unwanted nudges drive uninstalls, as Friend 2.0 and Omi showed. It ships only after citations prove reliable.

Briefs before you meet someone

Before a calendar event, show open items, promises and the last decisions from earlier conversations with the same people.

Seen inGranolaOtter.aiEven Realities G2 (with R1 ring)Flowtica VersoZocks

Why

This is the strongest repeat-use loop in meeting tools, and it is why transcripts are worth keeping longer than Recap's 7-day window.

Filter out media and split the day into conversations

Drop TV, music and podcasts using SoundAnalysis plus ShazamKit. Split the day into separate conversations so recaps read as events rather than one stream.

Seen inBee FrontierScribbleVetBOYA Notra

Why

The Verge found Bee treating TV and songs as conversation and leaking muted periods into summaries.

Unmetered local tier; pay only for cloud synthesis

Capture, on-iPhone transcription and on-device summaries are never metered and are sold free or as a one-time purchase. A subscription covers cloud synthesis, briefs, long retention and sync.

Seen inPocketComulytic Note ProPebble Index 01Just Press RecordWhisper NotesSpokenly

Why

Subscription fatigue is real (Bee Pro $11.99/mo, Omi Pro $29.99/mo), and minute caps punish long sessions. SpeechAnalyzer on the iPhone makes the marginal cost close to zero.

Later

Worth building once the core is reliable.

9 features

Ask from the wrist

Raise the wrist, ask, and get a cited one- or two-sentence answer from your own history, worked out on the iPhone.

Seen inPetey - AI Chat for Watch (formerly WatchGPT)Siri AI (Apple Intelligence, Gemini-based)Stream Ring

Why

Decision: Later, not Differentiator as Proposals 1 and 3 had it. The watch has no LLM, and sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is in the background, so the query path is unproven. PCC has quotas and needs a managed entitlement. Petey's 3.8 rating shows chat on the wrist is hard.

Outbound follow-ups with approval, a journal and undo

Draft emails, Slack recaps and CRM updates. Nothing sends without approval on the iPhone, and every action is journaled with its undo.

Seen inPlaud Note ProVocci AI Context RingCirclebackRead AI (Ada)Highlight AI

Why

High value, but acting on other people's words can do a lot of damage, and trust has to come first.

Session mode in the EEA, UK and Germany

Launch after a DPIA and a legal review of §201 StGB, with EU data residency. Until then only Memo ships there. When Sessions launch, the Core consent rules apply, plus explicit consent before capture.

Seen inJamietl;dvTandem HealthLimitless Pendant

Why

The EDPB statement, Germany's criminal penalties and Limitless's withdrawal from the EU and UK all show the risk.

Mac companion: meeting capture without a bot, heavier processing and full MCP

Core Audio process taps capture calls into the same vault. The Mac also runs full diarization (SpeakerKit, or FluidAudio with pyannote community-1) and WhisperKit, for more languages and custom vocabulary. It grows out of the v1.x Mac reader.

Seen inGranolaAnarlog (formerly Hyprnote)MacWhisperScreenpipePlaud NotePin S

Why

The heavier diarization tools are verified only on the Mac. It covers online meetings, but it is a second product surface in a crowded field (44 meeting notetakers in the catalog).

Phone-call capture with an announcement that can't be turned off

Record calls on the iPhone with an audible notice to every party.

Seen inPixel Call NotesTruecaller AI Call RecordingApple Voice Memos & Notes audio transcription (Apple Intelligence)Bee Eclipse

Why

Calls interrupt watch capture anyway, and they are the most regulated recording context. Apple, Pixel and Truecaller all announce the recording.

Consented voiceprints for regular contacts

A contact is named automatically only after they enroll their own voice and consent, and they can revoke it.

Seen inAI MindClipVibe DotJamie

Why

Bystander voiceprints may count as GDPR Art. 9 biometric data.

Place, calendar and health context on the timeline

Annotate conversations with visits, events, workouts and sleep or stress data.

Seen inTicNote WatchDay OneBee FrontierWhisper Memos

Why

Useful for recall and search, but it asks for more permissions and collects more data without improving core capture.

Templates, people pages, team mode and regulated-profession modes

Summary styles, pages built per person and project, admin policies for workplaces, and clinical, therapy and advisor modes.

Seen inPlaud NoteTwinMindFellowAbridgeUpheal

Why

Each one needs months of data or its own compliance work.

Instant replay and captions on watches without Live Rewind

Keep the last 15-30 seconds in memory and send that clip to the iPhone on request, with honest latency.

Seen inApple Watch Audio Intelligence (Siri Recap + Live Rewind)Live Transcribe & Sound NotificationsAirCaps (formerly TranscribeGlass)

Why

It helps accessibility, but it needs a fast round trip to speech recognition, and today's sync takes minutes.

The evidence

What the market already does

Patterns across 272 products

  • Capture and summarisation are commodities. cloud transcription appears in 211 of 272 products, tap or push-to-talk in 202 and automatic summaries in 165. All 26 AI voice recorders summarise, and 23 of them label speakers. Products now compete on takes actions for you (116), ask AI about your history (112) and searchable memory (111).
  • Deliberate capture outweighs ambient capture. tap or push-to-talk appears in 202 products and always-on capture in only 29, mostly pendants (11 of 18) and lifelogging platforms (7 of 8). Push-to-talk rings point the same way: Pebble Index 01 and Stream Ring are shipping, WIZPR Ring is in beta, and Natura Interface ring has not shipped. So does Plaud's press-to-record NotePin S. The Vocci AI Context Ring is the counterexample: a double-click starts up to 8 h of continuous recording.
  • The Apple Watch is underserved. Only 28 of 272 products flag Apple Watch app, and only 3 catalog entries are dedicated watch apps. Granola, Circleback, Bluedot and TwinMind each shipped a watch recorder only between Jun and Oct 2026.
  • Apple is now a direct competitor. Siri Recap gives summaries only, with no transcript or speaker labels, deleted after 7 days unless saved. Live Rewind shows the last 15 s as a transcript snippet. Both are free, in the watchOS 27.3 beta with release expected in December, and require a Series 12 or Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later. They work in English only and not in the EU.
