  • Trust tooling is a minority feature. Only 76 of 272 products have consent and recording controls (28%) and 59 have local-only or end-to-end privacy (22%). on-device transcription appears in 68 products against 211 for cloud transcription.
  • Integrations and agent access are now expected: third-party integrations appears in 162 products and export or API in 137. MCP ships in Granola, Omi, Pebble Index 01, Circleback, Monologue, Letterly, Whisper Memos, Otter.ai and Screenpipe.
  • Hardware recorders have converged on one offer: a $99-$249 device, a free tier of roughly 120-600 minutes a month, and a $100-$240 yearly upgrade. Free tiers: Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro Max 120 minutes; Plaud, AI MindClip and Vocci 300; TicNote and viaim 600. Challengers compete with free unlimited transcription (Pocket, Comulytic Note Pro, HiDock P1) or no subscription at all (Pebble Index 01 at $75).
  • Devices worn on the wrist or finger lean on haptics: 23 of 25 ring, watch and earbud products flag haptic or glanceable output, and 22 have tap-to-talk. TicNote Watch already sends summaries back to the wrist.
  • Many products die or slip. Six are discontinued (Humane Ai Pin, Limitless Pendant, Rewind, OpenGlass, Owl, Google Assistant), 22 are announced but unreleased, and 8 are rumored. Pickle 1's Q2 2026 Batch 1 target appears missed. IYO ONE missed its winter 2024 target and still says 'Ships TBD'. Plaud One Explorer's Q4 2026 deliveries are unconfirmed. iKairos missed its own pre-order window. Big tech is consolidating the field: Amazon bought Bee, Meta bought Limitless, HP bought Humane's assets, and Fathom joined Superhuman.
  • Proactive features are common (75 of 272) but backfire when nobody asked for them. Friend 2.0's unprompted texts read as intrusive, and Omi was called a 'micromanager' and removed its automatic reflections.

Gaps nobody fills well

  • Long capture that survives on the watches people already own. Apple limits Siri Recap to Series 12 and Ultra 4 with an iPhone 16 or later, which leaves out Series 9-11, SE 3 and Ultra 2-3. Third-party watch apps lose recordings (Omi lost 11 hours) and stop silently when interrupted. None shows which segments were delivered.
  • Output the user can check. Siri Recap gives summaries only, Live Rewind shows only the last 15 seconds, and Bee deletes audio. No product pairs a full transcript, me-vs-others labels, citations to transcript spans and a short window of audio for checking.
  • Honest coverage. No watch app shows receipts, gaps and 'not recorded' answers, or warns the user when the app itself has died, so users find holes only after the fact.
  • Status and results on the wrist. No third-party Apple Watch recorder shows the day's capture coverage, gaps and top items on the wrist. Siri Recap shows summaries only, and only on Series 12 and Ultra 4.
  • Consent tools that face the bystander, plus deletion on the spot. Only 76 of 272 products have consent controls. None offers bystanders a deletion route, and no watch recorder in the catalog gives the wearer a 'discard the last 15 minutes' control. A watch looks covert, so the wearer needs reminders to announce, logs and pause zones.
  • Memory the user owns and can take elsewhere. Only 59 of 272 products are local-only or end-to-end encrypted. Bulk export is missing in places (Voicenotes), and the Limitless and Humane shutdowns make an exit guarantee based on files a selling point.
  • Measured, honest battery budgets. Every continuous-recording figure in the category is a vendor claim, and no product shows drain measured on the user's own watch.
  • Languages beyond English, and records that last. Apple's features are English-only. Recap gives no full transcript, audio or export, and its summaries expire after 7 days unless saved one at a time. The EU follows only after legal review.

Research notes

Building on watchOS

The two briefs the recommendations are based on: what watchOS lets a third-party app do, and what existing Watch voice apps do and what their users say.

What watchOS allows: background audio, battery, speech, inputs, privacy

Brief: building an always-running voice-capture app for Apple Watch (as of 2026-11-16)

Confidence tags: [H] high, [M] medium, [L] low.

Platform baseline. The current release is watchOS 27.2.1, shipped Nov 9, 2026 (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/09/apple-releases-watchos-27-2-1/). watchOS 27.3 is in beta. watchOS 27 runs on Series 9 and later, Ultra 2 and later, and SE 3 (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/14/apple-releases-watchos-27/) [H]. Target watchOS 27 and keep a watchOS 26 fallback.

1. Background audio recording

  • Audio background mode is the only legitimate path for long recording. The user has to start the session while the app is in the foreground. It then keeps running in the background, and watchOS shows the app again whenever the wrist is raised (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/watchkit/enabling-background-sessions.md) [H].
    • Apple's documentation describes this mode in playback terms. Long-form playback needs a Bluetooth route (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/watchkit/playing-background-audio.md) [H].
    • An Apple Frameworks Engineer confirmed on the forums that recording keeps going after the app moves to the background. The same engineer said that "Recording cannot be resumed when the app is in the background on watchOS. It must be a user-initiated event while the app is in the foreground." A call or Siri therefore ends capture until the user reopens the app (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/750432) [H].
    • In that thread a developer asked whether App Review accepts long user-started recording. Apple did not answer [M].
    • Design consequence: never stop and restart the audio engine to save power. Keep the mic open and do the gating downstream [M].
  • WKExtendedRuntimeSession is no use for all-day capture. The four session types and limits are:
Session type Runs as Time limit
Self care Frontmost 10 min
Mindfulness Frontmost 1 h
Physical therapy Background 1 h
Smart alarm Background, schedulable 30 min

Each app gets one type. The session must start while the app is active. Apple says to pick the type "based on the app's intended use," and the system can cancel a session for sustained CPU use (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/watchkit/using-extended-runtime-sessions.md) [H].

  • HKWorkoutSession runs indefinitely but is a policy trap. Guideline 2.5.4 limits background services to their intended purposes (https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) [H]. One developer was rejected repeatedly for "improper use of HKWorkoutSession" (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/734323). Apple DTS defers these calls to App Review (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/773305). A workout session also moves the user's Activity rings [M]. Don't use it.
  • AudioRecordingIntent (watchOS 11+) makes the system show a recording indicator. Its documentation says that on watchOS you must keep a Live Activity running while recording (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents/audiorecordingintent.md). However, Activity.request lists only iOS and macOS (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/activitykit/activity/request(attributes:content:pushtype:).md). The behaviour on watch is unclear, so test on a device [L]. On iOS, developers report that a recording can't be cold-started from the background (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/815725) [M].

2. How existing watch recorders work

All of them use user-started sessions. None does true ambient, voice-triggered capture [M].

  • Omi: streams roughly 1-minute chunks to the iPhone. One 11 h 06 min session was lost. The fix adds a complete session file on the watch, crash recovery, and keeping chunks until the iPhone confirms receipt (https://github.com/BasedHardware/omi/issues/20479) [H].
  • Bee (Amazon): has a watch app (watchOS 10+). Its founders say watchOS limits mean the app "could never fully replicate" their wristband (https://www.androidauthority.com/bee-ai-wearable-3515345/) [M].
  • Limitless: acquired by Meta in December 2025 and the pendant discontinued. I found no watch app (https://www.usecarly.com/blog/meta-limitless-acquisition/) [M].
  • Whisper Memos: starts from a complication tap, works standalone, uploads over cellular, caps recordings at 90 min (https://whispermemos.com/features/start-recording/watch-complication) [M].
  • Just Press Record: has recorded in the background since watchOS 4 (https://www.applevis.com/apps/apple-watch/utilities/just-press-record) [L].
  • Wave: says it uses extended runtime sessions and auto-stops at 10% battery (https://wave.co/updates/wave-apple-watch-recording) [L].
  • Tiro: auto-stops below 25% battery or 50 MB free storage (https://docs.tiro.ooo/en/guide/recording/watch) [M].
  • Hedy: caps sessions at 4 h and reports about 3% battery per hour and about 10 MB per hour (https://www.aimeetingassistantreviews.com/blog/best-ai-note-taker-apple-watch/) [L, vendor claim].
  • Granola: starts with two taps on a complication and keeps recording with the screen dimmed (same source) [L].
  • Apple Siri Recap and Live Rewind: scheduled or ambient listening on Series 12 and Ultra 4 only. Audio is processed in the S11 Secure Exclave, transcribed on the iPhone, and summarised on PCC. They need an iPhone 16 or later, are in the watchOS 27.3 beta, English only, not in the EU or China, and 18+ (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148354) [H]. I found no third-party API (https://www.engadget.com/2304993/apples-latest-watchos-27-beta-enables-siri-recap-and-live-rewind-audio-features/) [M].

3. Battery

  • Rated battery life (normal / Low Power Mode):
Model Normal Low Power Mode
Series 11 24 h 38 h
Ultra 3 42 h 72 h
SE 3 18 h 32 h
Series 12 24 h 38 h
Ultra 4 50 h 84 h

Sources: https://www.macrumors.com/guide/buyers-guide-apple-watch-se-3-series-11-ultra-3/ and https://www.techrepublic.com/article/news-apple-watch-series-12-ultra-4/ [H]. Series 11 battery capacity is 1.245–1.403 Wh (https://www.macrumors.com/2025/09/12/apple-watch-series-11-increased-battery-catch/) [M].

  • No rigorous public measurement of mic drain exists. Vendor figures range from about 3%/h with the screen off (Hedy) to 15–20%/h, where a 2 h lecture takes 30–40% (https://speakwiseapp.com/blog/how-to-record-audio-apple-watch) [L].
  • My estimate of realistic hours from 100% to a 10–15% auto-stop [L, my own calculation]:
    • Series 11/12: about 10–14 h
    • SE 3: about 8–11 h
    • Ultra 3: about 18–24 h; Ultra 4 somewhat more
    • Wi-Fi/cellular streaming, screen-on time and on-watch ML all cut these figures.
  • Low Power Mode turns off the always-on display and background heart rate. Wi-Fi and cellular go off when the iPhone is away but come back when an app needs data. Background refresh runs less often (https://support.apple.com/HT213336) [M]. Whether recording works under Low Power Mode is untested here [L].
  • Apple's own Audio Intelligence claims no battery impact (https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/02/apple-watchs-ai-features-for-rewinding-and-recapping-conversations-begin-beta-testing/). That depends on S11 hardware [M].

4. On-device speech and AI on watchOS

  • No speech recognition on the watch:
    • SFSpeechRecognizer has no watchOS availability (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/sfspeechrecognizer.md) [H].
    • SpeechAnalyzer/SpeechTranscriber cover iOS, macOS, tvOS and visionOS 26, not watchOS (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/speech/speechanalyzer.md) [H].
    • The only option is system dictation through text-input UI, which returns final text only [M].
  • Foundation Models on watchOS 27 is cloud-only:
    • SystemLanguageModel (the on-device model) is not on watchOS (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel.md) [H].
    • PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel is, on watchOS 27+. It needs an entitlement and has per-user daily quotas (quotaLimitReached) (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/privatecloudcomputelanguagemodel.md) [H].
    • In Apple's watchOS group lab, Apple said: "There is no on-device model on the watch itself"; every call is a network hop to PCC; the paired iPhone isn't needed (https://jcalderita.com/wwdc26/watchos-group-lab/) [M].
    • The WWDC session confirms that PCC is what brings the framework to the watch (https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/241/) [H].
  • Voice activity detection (VAD) is possible on the watch. SoundAnalysis is available on watchOS 9+, and its built-in classifier covers 300+ sounds, including speech (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/soundanalysis.md) [H]. Core ML also runs on the watch. Whether third-party models get the Neural Engine is unconfirmed (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/738445) [L]. A cheap energy-based detector feeding a SoundAnalysis speech check is feasible [M].
  • Siri AI on watchOS 27 needs an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/14/apple-releases-watchos-27/) [H].

5. Data path

  • WCSession.transferFile is asynchronous, runs in the background, and is "throttle[d]...to accommodate performance and power." You can track it with outstandingFileTransfers. No size limit is published, and it doesn't work in the Simulator (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/watchconnectivity/wcsession/transferfile(_:metadata:).md) [H]. One developer reports a file under 30 MB failing on watchOS 10.5 (https://origin-devforums.apple.com/forums/thread/751623?page=2) [L]. Keep segments of 1–5 min, no more than a few MB each [M].
  • sendMessage fails when the iPhone app is backgrounded. Use transferUserInfo for control messages (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/762327) [M].
  • Low-level networking (Network framework, WebSockets) is allowed only while actively streaming audio, during a CallKit VoIP call, or for a DeviceDiscoveryUI connection to tvOS (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3135-low-level-networking-on-watchos.md) [H]. A developer measured the network path being revoked every ~36–38 s while an audio session is active. DTS tied this to repeated session activation and filed it as bug FB24377808 (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/841590) [M].
  • URLSession over cellular: background URLSession uploads may wait for Wi-Fi. DTS's suggestion is to upload with a standard session during runtime the app already has (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/843751) [M].

  • Storage and file sizes:

    • Storage is 64 GB on SE 3 (https://www.apple.com/sg/apple-watch-se-3/specs/) [H] and about 64 GB on current models [M].
    • Size per hour [H, arithmetic]:
    Format MB per hour
    AAC mono at 24 kbps ≈ 10.8
    AAC mono at 32 kbps ≈ 14.4
    LPCM 16 kHz / 16-bit ≈ 115
    • A 16 h day at 24–32 kbps AAC is about 175–230 MB.
    • Opus encoding on the watch is unverified. Older reports say only AAC and LPCM work (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/5653) [L]. Record AAC and transcode on the iPhone.

6. Input and UI affordances

  • Action Button (Ultra only). watchOS 26 Controls can be assigned to it on all Ultra models (https://www.macrumors.com/2025/06/15/watchos-26-custom-controls/) [H].
  • Controls in Control Center and the Smart Stack are new in watchOS 26. They run in the widget extension (https://charleswiltgen.github.io/Axiom/skills/watchos/controls-and-live-activities) [H]. Because capture must start in the foreground, a control should open the app [M].
  • Double Tap: use handGestureShortcut(.primaryAction). It works on S9 and later, including SE 3 with the S10 chip (https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/09/apple-introduces-apple-watch-se-3/). It doesn't work in Low Power Mode or with the wrist down (https://docs.tiro.ooo/en/guide/recording/watch) [H].
  • Wrist flick has no developer API. It is system-only (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/791574) [H].
  • The watchOS 27 single pinch selects Smart Stack widgets. I found no API for it [M].
  • Live Activities are started on the iPhone and mirrored to the watch Smart Stack [M].
  • Complications, Smart Stack widgets and RelevanceKit can be used for status and glanceable summaries [H].

7. Privacy and legal

  • Mic indicator: watchOS shows an orange mic icon whenever an app is using the microphone (https://support.apple.com/108038) [H].
  • App Store rules:
    • Guideline 2.5.14: "explicit user consent and... clear visual and/or audible indication when recording."
    • Guideline 5.1.2(i): disclose sharing with "third-party AI" and get explicit permission first.
    • Guideline 2.5.19: no hidden features.
    • Source: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ [H].
  • US recording law: federal law is one-party consent. About 11–13 states require all-party consent, including CA, FL, IL, WA, PA, MD and MA, with hybrids in OR, CT and MI (https://www.layer3labs.io/guides/two-party-consent-states) [M; secondary source, verify statutes].
  • EU: the EDPB smart-glasses statement (Oct 13, 2026) says:
    • The household exemption is narrow.
    • Manufacturers can't push GDPR duties onto users.
    • Recording indicators should be on by default and hard to disable.
    • Consent obtained after recording is invalid.
    • Source: https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2026-10/20261310_edpb_statement_smart-glasses_en.pdf [M].
  • Apple's own baseline for bystanders: Live Rewind plays a chime even when the watch is silenced and shows an animation. Siri Recap pauses during calls and FaceTime, omits sensitive data, and doesn't attribute speakers (https://support.apple.com/en-us/148354) [H]. The EFF has criticised Siri Recap (https://www.pcworld.com/article/3232402/will-siri-recap-make-the-apple-watch-creepy-privacy-experts-weigh-in.html) [M].
  • Workplace: recording at work needs employer policy and notice. Expect pushback on bystander privacy [M].

8. What's new in watchOS 26 and 27

  • watchOS 26: Controls, wrist flick (system-only), RelevanceKit, and arm64 on S9 and later (https://wwdcnotes.com/documentation/wwdc25-334-whats-new-in-watchos-26/) [H].
  • watchOS 27: Foundation Models via PCC, Vision on the watch, Siri AI, and Audio Intelligence on S12/U4 only (https://developer.apple.com/watchos/whats-new/) [H].
  • watchOS 27 can also offer to turn off gestures and Raise to Speak to save battery (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/14/apple-releases-watchos-27/) [M].

Feasibility verdict

Possible:

  • A user-started recording session that keeps running in the background for many hours with the screen off [H].
  • Voice detection on the watch to throw away silence [M].
  • Chunked AAC files queued to the iPhone, plus Wi-Fi/cellular upload when standalone [H].
  • Transcription on the iPhone with SpeechAnalyzer and on-device Foundation Models [H].
  • Summaries from the watch via PCC when online [H].
  • Starting from a complication, Control, Action Button (Ultra) or Double Tap inside the app [H].

Impossible or not allowed:

  • Starting or resuming capture without the user in the foreground: after a call or Siri interruption, a reboot, a crash, or on a schedule [H].
  • Siri Recap-style ambient listening using Apple's Secure Exclave hardware [H].
  • Speech-to-text on the watch through the Speech framework [H].
  • An on-device LLM on the watch [M].
  • Hiding the mic indicator [H].
  • Using a workout session for non-fitness recording [M].
  • A wrist-flick trigger [H].
  • Reliable WebSocket streaming [M].

Recommended capture architecture:

  1. Start: a "Start my day" tap from a complication, Control, Action Button or Double Tap. The app is in the foreground, shows a consent reminder, and activates AVAudioSession(.record or .playAndRecord). Activate once and never re-activate, because of the networking bug in section 5.
  2. Capture: an AVAudioEngine input tap feeding a ring buffer. A cheap energy-based detector, confirmed by the SoundAnalysis speech class, gates writing. The mic stays open; the gating is only at the encoder.
  3. Storage: AAC mono, 16 kHz, 24–32 kbps, in 1–5 min segment files, each flushed to disk and recorded in a journal.
  4. Sync: transferFile with receipts from the iPhone; delete a segment only after the iPhone confirms it. If the phone is unreachable, upload over URLSession.
  5. Phone side: transcribe with SpeechAnalyzer, summarise with Foundation Models, then push results back to Smart Stack widgets and complications.
  6. Interruptions: close the current segment, then send a time-sensitive notification with a haptic: "Tap to resume."
  7. Battery and storage guards: stop at 15% battery or under 100 MB free, and switch to a lower bitrate in Low Power Mode.
  8. Compliance:
    • Show an obvious in-app recording state and a one-tap pause ("bystander mode").
    • Show consent notices that depend on the user's jurisdiction.
    • Disclose any third-party AI and set clear retention and deletion policies.
Watch voice apps today, and what users praise and complain about

Apple Watch Voice Capture and AI: Market Scan (as of Nov 16, 2026)

Platform context (shapes every app)

  • Apple's own ambient AI is coming. watchOS 27.3 beta adds Live Rewind: double-press the Digital Crown to see a transcript of the last 15 seconds. It also adds Siri Recap, which listens in the background and writes a title, summary and key points but no transcript and no speaker labels. Summaries delete themselves after 7 days unless you save them. You can schedule Recap by time or place, or toggle it from Control Center. It runs through Private Cloud Compute, and raw audio stays in the S11 "Secure Exclave". Requirements: Series 12 or Ultra 4 plus an iPhone 16 or later, English only, not in the EU, with daily usage limits. Public release is expected in December (MacRumors, Apple Newsroom, 9to5Mac).
  • Third-party apps hit hard limits. watchOS has no public API for that kind of background capture. A recording interrupted by a call or Siri cannot resume while the app is in the background (Apple Dev Forums, thread 2). Since watchOS 8.1, a third-party app cannot open straight to dictation. System dictation stops silently after about 30–45 seconds (Drafts forum, timeout thread).

App-by-app

  1. Apple Voice Memos (watch). Free. Records on the watch and syncs over iCloud. The watch never shows text; transcription happens on iPhone and only when you trigger it (Speakwise, Apple). Complaints:
    • An hour-long recording reached the Mac as a few seconds (MPU forum).
    • Recordings stop when an alarm goes off (Apple Discussions).
  2. Apple Notes + Dictation (watchOS 26). Notes is new on the watch: dictate, scribble or type, synced through iCloud. Text only, with no audio transcription (Yahoo).
  3. Siri Recap / Live Rewind. Covered above. 9to5Mac's tester liked how much detail Recap caught, such as a table-runner size the family had mentioned (9to5Mac). Coverage calls it "controversial" for always listening and says sensitive details can still end up in summaries (TechCrunch, Tom's Guide).
  4. Bee (Amazon).
    • Listing: iPhone plus Apple Watch app, watchOS 10 or later, rated 4.8 from about 3K ratings. Bee Pro is $11.99/month or $99/year (App Store).
    • It started as an ambient recorder that captured everything unless you muted it (9to5Mac). After the acquisition, Bloomberg reportedly said recording now needs a button tap (tech-insider, secondary).
    • New hardware: Bee Frontier ($74.99, Oct 2026) and Bee Eclipse ($99.99, "soon"). Amazon lists Apple Watch as a Frontier integration and says no audio is stored (Amazon, Amazon help).
    • Complaints: frequent disconnects, a hallucinating model, summaries that "require some editing", no Mac access (App Store). Because audio is deleted you cannot replay it to check, and speaker labeling is weak (TechCrunch).
  5. Omi. The watch records when the Omi pendant isn't nearby; added in Oct 2025 (changelog). The pendant itself is $129 and records continuously (Omi). Complaints:
    • An 11-hour watch recording was lost (Featurebase).
    • Watch recordings never transferred, still unresolved more than a year later (Featurebase).
  6. Granola (launched Jul 28, 2026). Free, watchOS 11 or later (TechCrunch).
    • Capture: one tap or a complication. A green screen and a chime confirm it is recording, and it reminds you to get consent. Meeting nudges, offline capture.
    • Battery: Granola claims more than a dozen hour-long meetings per charge (Yahoo).
    • Complaints: the app must stay in the foreground, and recording stops if you check a text or set a timer. Sign-in is Google or Microsoft only (heise, HappyScribe).
    • Praise: a beta tester said the battery hit was minimal; others value the summaries; privacy worries remain (HN).
  7. Circleback (launched Jun 29, 2026). A complication starts in-person recording, which becomes notes, action items and a transcript. watchOS 10 or later. An Ultra Action Button shortcut arrived Oct 26 (Circleback, App Store).
  8. Whisper Memos.
    • Watch: works standalone and offline (uploads queue), up to 90 minutes, and the complication records without unlocking the watch.
    • AI: choice of Whisper, ElevenLabs or Cohere; custom-prompt summaries; "agents" that route a memo by name to email, tasks or Zapier. $69.99/year (site).
    • Rated 4.6 (454). Complaints: duplicate recordings, upload delays that clear only after opening the iPhone app, and a watch-app crash on Series 8 and older (since fixed) (App Store).
  9. Just Press Record. $6.99 one-time.
    • Watch: one-tap complication, unlimited length, standalone recording, records through AirPods from the watch, Double Tap, Smart Stack widget.
    • Transcription uses Apple's engine on iPhone (30+ languages); there are no AI summaries. Rated 4.3 (1.5K) (App Store).
    • Some users dropped it for free Voice Memos ("Sherlocked") (MPU).
  10. Voicenotes. watchOS 10.6 or later. Recently added an Action Button trigger, live transcription and dictation in any app. Rated 4.8 (7.3K). Plans: $8.99/week, $14.99/month, about $90–100/year (App Store). - Complaints: "stopped recording mid-session multiple times", summaries that never generate, no bulk export, inconsistent timestamps.
  11. Drafts. Four complication types (capture, capture with options, inbox count, flagged count). Dictation needs the phone or a network, and since watchOS 8 you must tap the mic first. Pro is $24.99/year (Drafts docs, Nemos). - Complaints: dictation transferred only in part, and sync broke after watchOS 11.6.1 (forum).
  12. Petey (formerly watchGPT). Standalone, with a complication; ask by voice or scribble, hear answers read aloud, send them to iPhone. Free tier with limits; Premium $6.99 or $59.99/year; or bring your own OpenAI key. Rated 3.8 (352) (App Store). - Complaints: confusion over buying versus needing an API key, flaky Digital Crown scrolling, a voice you can't change.
  13. Official ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. None of the three has a watch app. OpenAI's Dots (Sep 29, 2026) has no watch channel; only unofficial sideloaded clients exist (WatchDot, dot-watch), plus third-party apps such as Wrist AI and AskWatch (Agent Sonic, AskWatch, Wrist AI).
  14. AudioPen and Otter. I found no watchOS app for AudioPen. Otter's listing is iPhone and iPad only (Pro $16.99/month) (App Store).
  15. Newer entrants (2025–26). - Talk Memo ($3.99 one-time, May 2026): on-device transcription; Action Button, complication or Siri; routes to Notion, Obsidian or Bear (App Store). - Stardate: free, 100% local transcription (App Store). - WristNote: $14.99/month; a review reports transcriptions never arriving (App Store). - Pastok: sessions run in the background and can move to iPhone if the watch battery runs low; uploads directly (Pastok). - CraftNote: watch support since March 2026; free tier gives 2 hours a week (CraftNote). - Epiphany: one-tap "Actions" that route to Notion, Todoist, Slack or webhooks; transcription is in the cloud (Epiphany). - Nemos, Speakwise, Voice Notes (GlassFlag): auto-filing, offline queuing, and on-device Apple Intelligence summaries respectively (App Store).
  16. Non-watch comparison point: Plaud NotePin S. $179, physical button, up to 20 hours continuous, verbatim transcripts with speaker labels (Plaud).

(a) What people use watch voice capture for

  1. Quick capture: ideas, to-dos and reminders while walking, driving or working out (Whisper Memos, Talk Memo, Drafts).
  2. In-person meetings: walking one-on-ones, coffee chats, whiteboard sessions (Granola, Circleback).
  3. Ambient memory or lifelogging: "what did we decide?" (Bee, Omi, Siri Recap).
  4. Instant replay: "what did they just say?" (Live Rewind; accessibility).
  5. Journaling and reflection (Day One, Voicenotes).
  6. Hands-free routing into notes or task systems (Epiphany, Whisper Memos agents).
  7. Quick AI questions from the wrist (Petey).

(b) Top 10 recurring complaints

  1. Recordings lost or never transferred from watch to phone: Omi's 11-hour loss, Voice Memos truncation, Drafts after a watchOS update.
  2. Capture stops on interruption or when the app backgrounds: calls, Siri, alarms, screen lock (dev forums; Voicenotes "stopped mid-session").
  3. Watch is locked up while recording: Granola must stay in the foreground.
  4. Dictation is too short and dies silently (about 30–45 seconds), and third-party apps can't open straight to dictation.
  5. Processing and upload delays: you have to open the iPhone app; summaries that never arrive (Whisper Memos, WristNote, Voicenotes).
  6. Hard-to-trust AI output: hallucinations, edits needed, and no audio to check against (Bee; Siri Recap gives summaries only).
  7. Weak or missing speaker attribution (Bee, Siri Recap).
  8. Pricing friction: weekly plans, prices that don't match the listing, API-key confusion (Petey), fear of later price hikes.
  9. Privacy, consent and legal risk: wiretap-law questions (Quartz), always-listening unease.
  10. Battery uncertainty and hardware or region gating: almost nothing has been measured, Series 12 is rated at about 24 hours (BGR), and Recap is limited to new hardware, English, and outside the EU.

(c) Features users love most

  • One tap to start, from a complication, the Action Button, Double Tap or Smart Stack, ideally with no unlock (Whisper Memos, Just Press Record, Talk Memo).
  • Standalone and offline capture that uploads automatically later.
  • Long or unlimited recording.
  • Accurate transcription with model choice.
  • Automatic routing to email, Drafts, Obsidian, Notion or Zapier.
  • Clear recording feedback: chime, haptic, color, plus a consent prompt.
  • Pay once or a generous free tier.
  • On-device privacy (Stardate, Talk Memo).
  • Ambient recall that surfaces details people missed (Siri Recap).

(d) Unmet needs and gaps

  • Always-on capture on older watches that survives backgrounding and interruptions; Apple's version is limited to new hardware and new phones.
  • A choice of what to keep: summary only, transcript, or transcript plus audio, with per-situation retention.
  • Guaranteed delivery: visible queue status, receipts, retries; no silent loss.
  • Record while using the rest of the watch.
  • One-tap dictation into any app without the 45-second cap.
  • Reviewing on the wrist: search or ask your memories from the watch; today it is capture only.
  • Speaker ID and consent tooling for two-party-consent states.
  • Battery-aware modes: voice-activity gating, published drain numbers.
  • Coverage gaps: EU and non-English support; official ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude on the wrist.
  • Open export and cross-app memory: bulk export, and memory that isn't locked inside Bee or Omi.

Risks and open questions

  • App Review may treat the audio background mode as playback-only. One developer was rejected for exactly that (forum 776949), Apple did not answer the question about long recording (forum 750432), and DTS cannot speak for App Review. This decides whether the product can exist. Mitigations: TestFlight first, Meet with Apple, user-started time-boxed Sessions, an obvious recording state, no keep-alives, and never saying 'always listening'.
  • Apple could widen Siri Recap and Live Rewind to older watches, more languages, the EU, transcripts or an API in any point release. No third-party API exists. On Series 12 and Ultra 4, nobody has tested whether our session and Apple's compete for the mic. The durable defences are the user-owned vault, file export, consent tooling and agent access.
  • Battery drain has never been measured. If real drain is near the 15-20 %/h vendors report, Series and SE users get half-day Sessions and the pitch shrinks to 'meetings only'. The recording screen appears on every wrist raise, and its cost is unmeasured. The CPU cost of SoundAnalysis and recording under Low Power Mode are also untested. Measure per model against the per-model gates in week one, before making any claim.
  • Interruptions cannot be recovered without a tap. Calls, Siri, alarms and apps that use audio all end capture. Heavy phone users will have many gaps and may tire of resume nudges, so real coverage could fall well short of 'a workday'. The dead-man notification catches silent deaths, but it adds one more alert.
  • Sync is fragile. The OS throttles transferFile, and one report describes a file under 30 MB failing. Background transfers may wait for Wi-Fi, and the network path is revoked every ~36-38 s during audio sessions (FB24377808). CloudKit uploads from a watch in a background audio session are unverified. This needs the ledger, soak tests per watch model, and tests with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off.
  • The iPhone side is unverified. Long SpeechAnalyzer jobs may not fit within BGProcessingTask or BGContinuedProcessingTask limits, so transcripts may wait for charging or for the app to be opened. The watch shows 'Waiting for iPhone' instead of pretending, but the 'summaries never arrive' complaint could return.
  • Wearer separation may fail its 95% precision gate on wrist audio, since diarization is verified only on the Mac. If it fails, strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consent keep only summaries of what others said, which weakens the verifiable-record pitch in 14 states.
  • Wrist-mic audio quality is unknown. Pickup across a table, clothing rustle and sleeve occlusion have not been compared with multi-mic devices (Plaud Note Pro has 4 mics, Comu Action Pro 6). SpeechTranscriber's WER of 14.0 on earnings22 is a Mac benchmark, not wrist audio.
  • Legal exposure. Brewer v. Otter.ai and Subia v. Meta are verified, and pleading-stage rulings in early 2026 mostly favoured plaintiffs. Relevant rules: 13 all-party-consent states plus Michigan's hybrid rule, EDPB Statement 01/2026, and up to 3 years' imprisonment under §201 StGB. California's SB 1130 indicator mandate was vetoed and may return. Workplaces may ban recording. Discard and summary-only retention reduce exposure but do not cure interception claims. This is not legal advice: get counsel before an EU launch or workplace marketing.
  • Social rejection. A watch looks covert, and the press called Bee the 'creepiest Apple Watch app' and Siri Recap a 'passive surveillance state'. A recording screen that replaces the watch face for hours may irritate wearers. Announce through a tiny watch speaker is often inaudible, so in practice it depends on the wearer saying it. If announcing and pause zones aren't used, users drop social settings first, as the long-term Limitless user did.
  • Wrong attributions and hallucinations. One wrong 'you promised X' on the wrist does lasting damage, and summaries could be misused as evidence. Mitigate with citations, uncertainty labels, media filtering and a self-check before anything reaches the watch.
  • Pause semantics. The orange indicator stays lit while the screen says 'Paused', and bystanders may not believe it. Asking before resuming and switching to Stop after 10 unanswered minutes reduce the ambiguity. Stop must still be offered whenever someone objects.
  • Platform details that need device verification: - ADTS writing on watchOS. - Whether completeUnlessOpen lets segment writes continue after the watch locks. - Chime playback in Silent Mode and with AirPods connected, and how .playAndRecord routes. - Whether Double Tap and notification actions reliably bring the app forward during a background session. - Whether the user can leave the app for the watch face during a Session. - transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo with WidgetKit complications, and widget reload budgets. - How coarse batteryLevel readings are, and whether volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey exists on watchOS. - Any lock or off-wrist signal. - AudioRecordingIntent's Live Activity requirement. - The watchOS 26 device list for the fallback.
  • Cloud privacy promises depend on Anthropic confirmations. Batch ZDR eligibility is unconfirmed. The target of the server-side fallback must stay within the ZDR arrangement. The vendor's organization needs a ZDR arrangement in place. Users who bring their own key fall outside it. Until these are confirmed, the promise covers only standard Messages requests through App Attest or a stateless proxy.
  • Economics. Competitors offer free unlimited transcription (Pocket, Comulytic Note Pro, HiDock P1), $75 hardware with no subscription (Pebble Index 01), or a $74.99 device tied into Alexa+ (Bee Frontier). Local processing is a cost necessity, and the 4,096-token context of Foundation Models limits summary quality on the free tier.
  • Our own continuity. An acquisition or shutdown would repeat Limitless. Scheduled file exports, the published schema and the open-source reader mitigate this, but users who never export are exposed. The product must work locally without an account.
  • Evidence quality. Single-source or vendor claims: all battery figures, Chamberlain v. Granola (do not cite externally), Bee requiring a button tap after the Amazon acquisition, and wearer-only isolation in the unshipped Nirva and Taya. Sources also conflict on whether Granola keeps recording while other apps are open. Where the catalog (Nov 16) and the Earshot notes (Nov 14) disagreed, I used the catalog: Stream Ring is shipping (Earshot: preorder), and Pebble Index 01 is $75 and in stock (Earshot: $99). Catalog records marked unchecked were not re-verified.

How this was put together

Twelve research agents each searched the live web for one part of the market: pendants and pins, recorders, glasses, rings and earbuds, meeting notetakers, voice-note apps, dictation tools, voice assistants, Apple Watch apps, professional scribes, lifelogging platforms, and launches due in the next few months. That produced 314 raw records. Duplicates and off-topic entries were removed, gaps were filled, and records were fact-checked in batches of ten against current sources. Products listed as upcoming, rumored or in beta got one more check that tried to disprove the claimed status and date.

Of the 272 products, 126 were fact-checked a second time: 85 with high confidence, 40 medium and 1 low. The second check covered every pendant, recorder, ring, watch and earbud, every Apple Watch app, every lifelogging platform, and everything upcoming, rumored, in beta or discontinued. The remaining 146 are shipping software (meeting notetakers, scribes, dictation tools, assistants, voice-note apps and glasses) that the research sweep found and sourced but that were not re-checked, because the run reached the account's usage limit. Each catalog entry says which group it is in. 0 records were dropped because they could not be confirmed.

A feature counts only when a source confirms it, so a missing feature can mean "not documented" as well as "not offered". Prices and dates change often. Check the linked sources before relying on a specific figure.

Three reviewers drafted the feature sets independently, one focused on user value, one on watchOS feasibility and battery, one on privacy and market position. A fourth merged them, and a final reviewer checked the merged version against the research and fixed what did not hold up.

Review notes: what changed after critique, and how source conflicts were settled

Changes made after review:

  • Audio retention now depends on jurisdiction and consent. In strict jurisdictions without logged consent, audio is shredded as soon as transcription succeeds.
  • Sensitive filters now run on transcripts, and the audio of a flagged span is shredded immediately.
  • The exit guarantee rests on exported files, not CloudKit.
  • MCP moves to v1.x, served by a minimal signed Mac reader.
  • Battery gates and claims are set per watch model.

Where sources conflicted, I chose the more specific, better-sourced claim and name the choice in the item:

  • the Nov 16 catalog over the Nov 14 Earshot notes
  • DTS guidance over always using background uploads
  • Apple's own 18+ rule
  • Kilpatrick's 13 all-party-consent states plus Michigan
